definition_zh: 贡献；捐款；来稿；促成作用
definition_en: something given to help a shared purpose, or the act of giving it
core_image: 一只罐子里叠着许多不同面额的硬币
scene: 会后名单贴在墙上，每个名字后面写着金额。Her contribution made the project possible.
sceneCN: 这里 contribution 指「捐款」（第 2 个义项：为某项事业拿出的款项）；句意是她的捐款让这个项目得以启动。

pos.zh: 贡献；捐款；来稿；促成作用

senses.title: A share given
senses.definition: something valuable that a person gives to a shared effort
senses.definitionCN: 个人为共同事业拿出的有价值之物
senses.example: Her contribution to the team was never forgotten.
senses.exampleCN: 她对团队的贡献从未被忘记。
senses.why: A group remembers what one pair of hands added.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体会记住某一双手添了什么。

senses.title: Money given
senses.definition: a sum of money given to a cause or a group
senses.definitionCN: 为某项事业或团体拿出的款项
senses.example: The school asked for a small contribution.
senses.exampleCN: 学校请求大家小额捐款。
senses.why: Coins in a box become a building in time.
senses.whyCN: 盒子里的硬币，久了会变成一座楼。

senses.title: A piece written
senses.definition: a text sent to a paper, magazine or collection
senses.definitionCN: 寄给报刊或文集的文章
senses.example: The magazine printed four contributions.
senses.exampleCN: 杂志刊出了四篇来稿。
senses.why: A page is a meeting place, not a single voice.
senses.whyCN: 一个版面是聚会的场所，不只是一个人的声音。

intro.en: Contribution comes from Latin contributio, a bringing together of shares, from contribuere, built on com-, together, and tribuere, to allot.
intro.cn: contribution 来自拉丁语 contributio（各份的汇集），源于 contribuere，由 com-（一起）与 tribuere（分配）构成。

items.en: Tribuere meant to assign a part to each person.
items.cn: tribuere 意为给每人分配一份。

items.en: Contribuere meant to bring those parts into one place.
items.cn: contribuere 意为把各份带到一个地方。

items.en: Contributio named the common fund so formed.
items.cn: contributio 指这样形成的公库。

items.en: French contribution kept the sense of a paid share.
items.cn: 法语 contribution 保留了缴付一份的意思。

items.en: English contribution widened to effort and writing.
items.cn: 英语 contribution 扩大到力气与文字。

items.en: It now also names a single act of helping.
items.cn: 如今它也指一次具体的帮忙。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin allotting base tribut-, and the meaning group names other words for what is given to a shared end.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的分配词基 tribut-，近义组列出其他表示为共同目标给出的东西。

entries.definition: to give a share to a common purpose
a person who gives or writes for others
the handing out of things to many people
money or goods given to a cause
something put in to help a process
a part that belongs to one person

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with value added by one pair of hands, then move to coins in a box and an article sent to a page.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一双添上的手开始，再到盒子里的硬币，最后到寄给版面的文章。

normal.en: Contribution is the noun behind contribute: the thing you put in.
normal.cn: contribution 是 contribute 背后的名词：你放进去的那样东西。

normal.en: A team remembers the one who carried the water.
normal.cn: 一个团队会记住那个挑水的人。

normal.en: Small coins in a box become walls in time.
normal.cn: 盒子里的零钱，日子久了会变成墙。

normal.en: An article is also a dish on a shared table.
normal.cn: 一篇文章也是公共餐桌上的一道菜。

normal.en: Give a part, and the whole is different.
normal.cn: 给出一份，整体就不一样了。

abstract.en: Picture one coin resting on a tall pile.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币落在高高的一堆上。

abstract.en: Picture a name written under a given sum.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字写在一笔金额之下。

abstract.en: Picture many pens filling one printed page.
abstract.cn: 想象许多支笔写满同一个版面。

examples.en: He made a real contribution to the research.
examples.cn: 他对这项研究作出了真正的贡献。

examples.en: A small contribution from each member was enough.
examples.cn: 每位成员捐一点就够了。

examples.en: The paper welcomes contributions from readers.
examples.cn: 这份报纸欢迎读者来稿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 contribution 记成 contribute（贡献）加 ion（名词尾）：大家各出一份凑起来的那个东西，就是贡献。

root: 源自拉丁语 contributio（各份的汇集），来自 contribuere（把份额凑到一起），由 con-（一起）与 tribuere（分配）构成。

sensesIntro.en: From a valuable share, to a sum of money, and at last to a piece of writing sent to a page.
sensesIntro.cn: 从有价值的一份，到一笔钱，最后到寄给版面的文字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one coin laid on a tall stack of coins.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币放在高高的一摞硬币上。

branches.en: The widest sense covers any valuable share.
branches.cn: 最宽的义项涵盖任何有价值的一份。

branches.en: Money is the shape this share most often takes.
branches.cn: 钱是这一份最常见的形状。

branches.en: A written piece is a share of words.
branches.cn: 一篇文字是文字上的一份。

branches.en: Effort and money both fill the same pool.
branches.cn: 力气和钱都往同一个池子里倒。

branches.en: A gift and a column both reach other people.
branches.cn: 捐款与专栏最后都到了别人手里。

intro.en: Contribution is built on contribute plus the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: contribution 由 contribute 加名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The allotting base tribut- also appears in tribute, distribute and attribute.
latinIntro.cn: 分配词基 tribut- 也出现在 tribute、distribute 与 attribute 中。

items.meaning: the share that has been given
items.exampleCN: 这笔捐助被记录了下来。

items.example: The delay was a contributory cause.
They paid tribute to the old teacher.

items.meaning: to give a cause to something
items.example: He attributes the win to practice.

definition_zh: 控制；管理；抑制；控制装置
definition_en: the power to make something act as you wish, or to keep it within limits, or a device that steers a machine
core_image: 一只手握着方向盘，车随着掌心转向
scene: 雨天路滑，司机双手稳稳压住方向盘。He kept the car under control on the wet road.
sceneCN: 这里 control 指「控制」（第 1 个义项：让某物按自己意愿行动的能力）；句意是在湿滑的路面上，他把车控制得很稳。

senses.title: Power to direct
senses.definition: the ability to make something act as one wishes
senses.definitionCN: 让某物按自己意愿行动的能力
senses.example: She has no control over the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 她对预算没有控制权。
senses.why: A horse follows the hand that holds the rein.
senses.whyCN: 马跟着握缰绳的那只手走。

senses.title: To keep in limits
senses.definition: to keep something from growing too large or dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物不至于过大或危险
senses.example: Firefighters controlled the fire before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员在天亮前控制住了火势。
senses.why: A small flame in the palm is easier than a field on fire.
senses.whyCN: 掌心里的小火苗，比一片火场好对付。

senses.title: A device that steers
senses.definition: a switch or handle used to operate a machine
senses.definitionCN: 用来操作机器的开关或把手
senses.example: The volume control is on the left.
senses.exampleCN: 音量控制键在左边。
senses.why: Where the hand rests, the machine listens.
senses.whyCN: 手停在哪儿，机器就听哪儿。

intro.en: Control comes from Medieval Latin contrarotulus, a copy of a roll checked against the original, from contra-, against, and rotulus, a little roll.
intro.cn: control 来自中世纪拉丁语 contrarotulus（与正本核对用的副本），由 contra-（对照）与 rotulus（小卷轴）构成。

items.en: Rotulus meant a small roll of writing.
items.cn: rotulus 意为一小卷书写物。

items.en: Contrarotulus was a second roll kept for checking.
items.cn: contrarotulus 是为核对而保留的第二份卷轴。

items.en: French contrerole named the register used in checking accounts.
items.cn: 法语 contrerole 指核对账目所用的登记册。

items.en: English control first meant a check kept on money.
items.cn: 英语 control 最初指对钱财的核查。

items.en: The word widened to mean power over anything.
items.cn: 这个词扩大到指对任何事物的支配力。

items.en: It also names the switches that steer machines.
items.cn: 它也指操纵机器的开关。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the control family, and the meaning group names other verbs for directing and limiting.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 control 词族的成员，近义组列出其他表示支配与限制的动词。

entries.definition: a person or device that directs something
kept within fixed limits
not kept within limits
to direct people or work successfully
to keep something at a steady level
to order and direct with authority

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a hand on the rein, then move to a fire kept small and a switch that the machine obeys.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从握着缰绳的手开始，再到被压小的火，最后到机器听从的开关。

normal.en: Control first meant a check copy, so the idea of keeping watch is old.
normal.cn: control 最初指核对用的副本，所以盯住不放的意思很古老。

normal.en: The hand on the rein decides where the horse goes.
normal.cn: 握缰绳的手决定马往哪里走。

normal.en: A fire is controlled by making it smaller, not bigger.
normal.cn: 控制火势靠把它弄小，而不是弄大。

normal.en: The switch is where the whole machine listens.
normal.cn: 开关就是整台机器听话的地方。

normal.en: No hand, no direction.
normal.cn: 没有手，就没有方向。

abstract.en: Picture one hand closing gently on a rein.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻轻握住缰绳。

abstract.en: Picture a flame shrinking under a metal cup.
abstract.cn: 想象火苗在金属杯下缩小。

abstract.en: Picture a row of dials under a single thumb.
abstract.cn: 想象一排旋钮都在一根拇指之下。

examples.en: The driver lost control of the truck.
examples.cn: 司机失去了对卡车的控制。

examples.en: They controlled the crowd with a low fence.
examples.cn: 他们用一道矮栏控制住人群。

examples.en: The control for the light is by the door.
examples.cn: 灯的开关在门边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 control 记成 contra（对照）加 rol（卷轴）：拿一份副本对着正本逐条核对，就是掌控与节制。

root: 源自中世纪拉丁语 contrarotulus（核对用的副本卷轴），由 contra-（对照）与 rotulus（小卷轴）构成，后指支配、抑制与控制装置。

sensesIntro.en: From the power to direct, to keeping a danger small, and at last to the switch where the machine listens.
sensesIntro.cn: 从支配的力量，到把危险压小，最后到机器听话的那个开关。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand closing on a rein.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢在缰绳上。

branches.en: Power over motion is the central sense.
branches.cn: 对运动的主导是核心义项。

branches.en: Power also means keeping a danger small.
branches.cn: 这种力量也意味着把危险压小。

branches.en: The switch is power made into an object.
branches.cn: 开关是把力量做成了一个物件。

branches.en: Directing and limiting are two sides of one hand.
branches.cn: 主导与限制是同一只手的两面。

branches.en: A dial can hold a process inside safe limits.
branches.cn: 一个旋钮能把过程限制在安全范围内。

intro.en: Control is built on Latin contra-, against, plus rotulus, a little roll.
intro.cn: control 由拉丁语 contra-（对照）与 rotulus（小卷轴）构成。

latinIntro.en: The roll base rot- also appears in rotate, rotation and rotary.
latinIntro.cn: 卷轴词基 rot- 也出现在 rotate、rotation 与 rotary 中。

items.meaning: to check one roll against another
items.meaningCN: 用一份卷轴核对另一份
起支配或调节作用的人或物

items.meaning: able to be kept in limits
items.exampleCN: 这场火是可以控制住的。

items.meaningCN: 被限制在设定范围内的

items.exampleCN: 她表现出很强的自制力。

items.meaning: to keep at a steady level

definition_en: easy to use, reach or fit into a plan
core_image: 地铁口正对着小区大门
scene: 出门两分钟就到车站，买菜也不用过马路。The flat is convenient for the station.
sceneCN: 这里 convenient 指「近便的」（第 1 个义项：距离近或程序简单而省力）；句意是这套公寓去车站很方便。

senses.title: Easy to reach
senses.definition: near enough or simple enough to save effort
senses.definitionCN: 距离够近或程序够简单而省力
senses.example: The hotel is convenient for the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店去机场很方便。
senses.why: Nearness is measured in effort, not in metres.
senses.whyCN: 远近是按力气算的，不是按米算的。

senses.title: Fitting the plan
senses.definition: arranged at a time or in a way that suits someone
senses.definitionCN: 在时间或方式上适合某人的
senses.example: Let us meet at a convenient hour.
senses.exampleCN: 我们挑个合适的时间见面吧。
senses.why: A good hour is one nobody has to fight the clock for.
senses.whyCN: 好的时间，是没人需要和钟表较劲的时间。

senses.title: Handy for use
senses.definition: designed to be simple to operate
senses.definitionCN: 设计得容易操作
senses.example: The handle is at a convenient height.
senses.exampleCN: 把手的高度正合适使用。
senses.why: A tool should meet the hand halfway.
senses.whyCN: 工具应当朝手走一半路。

intro.en: Convenient comes from Latin convenire, to come together or fit, built on com-, together, and venire, to come.
intro.cn: convenient 来自拉丁语 convenire（走到一起、相合），由 com-（一起）与 venire（来）构成。

items.en: Venire meant to come near or arrive.
items.cn: venire 意为靠近或到达。

items.en: Convenire meant to meet and to fit together.
items.cn: convenire 意为相遇，也指彼此相合。

items.en: The participle conveniens described what fits well.
items.cn: 分词 conveniens 形容恰好相合的事物。

items.en: French convenant kept the sense of suitable.
items.cn: 法语 convenant 保留了合适之义。

items.en: English convenient meant fitting and handy.
items.cn: 英语 convenient 指合适而顺手。

items.en: It now mostly means easy to reach or use.
items.cn: 如今它多指容易到达或使用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin coming base ven-, and the meaning group names other words for what suits a need.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的来词基 ven-，近义组列出其他表示合于需要的词。

entries.definition: the state of being easy to use
in an easy or suitable way
causing trouble or extra effort
easy to use or close at hand
right for a particular purpose
easy to reach or enter

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a short walk, then move to a good hour and a handle at the right height.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一小段路开始，再到一个好时辰，最后到高度正好的把手。

normal.en: Convenient is the adjective of convenience: it fits your need.
normal.cn: convenient 是 convenience 的形容词：它合你的需要。

normal.en: If the walk is short, the place is convenient.
normal.cn: 路短，地方就方便。

normal.en: A good hour is one that does not fight your clock.
normal.cn: 好的时间，是不跟你的钟表作对的时间。

normal.en: A handle at the right height is convenience in wood.
normal.cn: 高度合适的把手，是木头做成的方便。

normal.en: It fits, so it saves.
normal.cn: 它合得上，所以省力气。

abstract.en: Picture a station door right across the street.
abstract.cn: 想象街对面就是车站的门。

abstract.en: Picture a chair pulled up to a low table.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子正好拉到矮桌旁。

abstract.en: Picture a key already in the lock.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙已经插在锁里。

examples.en: The flat is convenient for the school.
examples.cn: 这套公寓去学校很方便。

examples.en: Is this a convenient time to talk?
examples.cn: 现在方便谈话吗？

examples.en: The tool is light and convenient to use.
examples.cn: 这件工具轻便好用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 convenient 记成 con（一起）加 ven（来）加 ient：需要的东西恰好在身边来到，就是方便的。

root: 源自拉丁语 convenire（走到一起、相合），由 com-（一起）与 venire（来）构成，加形容词词尾 -ient，指近便、合适与好用。

sensesIntro.en: From a short distance, to a fitting hour, and at last to a tool that meets the hand.
sensesIntro.cn: 从很短的距离，到合适的时辰，最后到朝手迎上来的工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a station door directly across the street.
core.cn: 核心意象：街对面就是车站的门。

branches.en: Short distance is the plainest kind of ease.
branches.cn: 短距离是最朴素的省力。

branches.en: A fitting hour removes a different kind of effort.
branches.cn: 合适的时间去掉另一种力气。

branches.en: A well-made tool meets the body halfway.
branches.cn: 做得好用的工具朝身体走了一半。

branches.en: Space and time can both be made to fit.
branches.cn: 空间与时间都能被安排得合身。

branches.en: A good hour and a good handle both say yes.
branches.cn: 好时辰与好把手都在说可以。

intro.en: Convenient is built on Latin com-, together, plus venire, to come.
intro.cn: convenient 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 venire（来）构成。

latinIntro.en: The coming base ven- also appears in convenience, convene and convention.
latinIntro.cn: 来词基 ven- 也出现在 convenience、convene 与 convention 中。

items.meaningCN: 聚会或共同接受的习俗
双方之间有约束力的约定

definition_en: a usual way of doing things, a formal agreement, or a large organized meeting
core_image: 会场里一排排座位，人人按同一套规矩行事
scene: 年会在大厅举行，代表们按名牌落座。The party holds its convention every autumn.
sceneCN: 这里 convention 指「大会」（第 3 个义项：团体或行业的大型正式会议）；句意是这个政党每年秋天举行大会。

senses.title: An accepted habit
senses.definition: a way of behaving that most people in a group accept
senses.definitionCN: 群体中多数人接受的做事方式
senses.example: Shaking hands is a convention, not a law.
senses.exampleCN: 握手是惯例，不是法律。
senses.why: A crowd repeats a habit until it feels like a rule.
senses.whyCN: 一群人反复做一件事，久了就像规定。

senses.title: A formal agreement
senses.definition: a set of rules agreed by many parties
senses.definitionCN: 由多方共同议定的规则集合
senses.example: The treaty follows an older convention.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约沿用了更早的公约。
senses.why: Nations write down what they hope to keep.
senses.whyCN: 国家把希望守住的东西写下来。

senses.title: A large meeting
senses.definition: a big organized meeting of a group or profession
senses.definitionCN: 团体或行业的大型正式会议
senses.example: Thousands came to the yearly convention.
senses.exampleCN: 数千人来参加年度大会。
senses.why: A field of strangers becomes one body for a few days.
senses.whyCN: 一群陌生人在几天里变成一个整体。

intro.en: Convention comes from Latin convenire, to come together, built on com-, together, and venire, to come.
intro.cn: convention 来自拉丁语 convenire（走到一起），由 com-（一起）与 venire（来）构成。

items.en: Venire meant to come or arrive.
items.cn: venire 意为来或到达。

items.en: Convenire meant to meet and to agree with one another.
items.cn: convenire 意为会面，也指彼此取得一致。

items.en: Conventio named a coming together and the agreement made.
items.cn: conventio 指聚到一起以及由此达成的约定。

items.en: French convention kept both the meeting and the custom senses.
items.cn: 法语 convention 同时保留聚会与习俗两层意思。

items.en: English convention meant an agreed custom.
items.cn: 英语 convention 指共同接受的习俗。

items.en: It now also means a large professional gathering.
items.cn: 如今它也指大型的行业聚会。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin coming base ven-, and the meaning group names other words for custom and assembly.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的来词基 ven-，近义组列出其他表示习俗与集会的词。

entries.definition: following the usual accepted way
to call people together for a meeting
the quality of being easy to use
a usual way of behaving in a society
a belief or habit passed down over years
a group of people gathered for a purpose

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a habit a crowd repeats, then move to rules written by many parties and a hall full of strangers.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从人群反复做的习惯开始，再到多方写下的规则，最后到坐满陌生人的大厅。

normal.en: Con- is together and ven is come, so a convention is people coming together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，ven 是来，convention 就是人们来到一起。

normal.en: When enough people come together, their habit becomes the rule.
normal.cn: 来的人够多，他们的习惯就成了规矩。

normal.en: Nations meet, and the paper they sign is also a convention.
normal.cn: 国家相聚，签下的那张纸也叫公约。

normal.en: A hall of name cards is the meeting sense made visible.

normal.en: Come together, agree, and repeat.

abstract.en: Picture a long table with many pens beside one page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，许多支笔放在同一页纸旁。

abstract.en: Picture a hall of chairs turned toward one stage.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅里所有椅子都朝向同一个舞台。

examples.en: By convention, the host speaks first.
examples.cn: 按照惯例，主人先发言。

examples.en: The two countries signed a convention on trade.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 convention 记成 con（一起）加 ven（来）加 tion：大家来到一起、说定一套做法，就是惯例与大会。

root: 源自拉丁语 conventio（聚会与约定），来自 convenire（走到一起），由 con-（一起）与 venire（来）构成，后指习俗、公约与大会。

sensesIntro.en: From a habit a crowd accepts, to rules written by many parties, and at last to a hall of people gathered.
sensesIntro.cn: 从人群接受的习惯，到多方写下的规则，最后到聚满人的大厅。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hall of chairs all turned toward one stage.
core.cn: 核心意象：大厅里所有椅子都朝向同一个舞台。

branches.en: The habit sense grows out of repeated agreement.
branches.cn: 惯例义从反复的一致中长出来。

branches.en: The written sense puts that agreement on paper.
branches.cn: 书面义把这种一致放到纸上。

branches.en: The meeting sense gathers the people themselves.
branches.cn: 大会义把人本身聚起来。

branches.en: A custom and a treaty are both agreed rules.
branches.cn: 习俗与条约都是议定的规则。

branches.en: People who write rules must first come together.
branches.cn: 写规则的人，总要先聚到一起。

intro.en: Convention is built on Latin com-, together, plus venire, to come.

latinIntro.en: The coming base ven- also appears in convene, convenient and event.
latinIntro.cn: 来词基 ven- 也出现在 convene、convenient 与 event 中。

items.meaning: a coming together and what is agreed
items.meaningCN: 聚到一起以及所议定的事

items.meaning: a way by which one comes
items.example: The avenue was lined with trees.

items.meaning: to come before and stop something
items.meaningCN: 先一步到来并加以阻止

definition_en: following the usual and accepted way of doing things
core_image: 一整排相同的窗子，尺寸和间距都一样
scene: 邻居都装同样的白窗帘，只有她挂了一块彩布。Her house stands out among the conventional ones.
sceneCN: 这里 conventional 指「传统的」（第 1 个义项：按多数人接受的方式行事）；句意是她的房子在那些传统样式的房子中格外显眼。

senses.title: Following custom
senses.definition: acting in the way most people in a society accept
senses.definitionCN: 按社会多数人接受的方式行事
senses.example: They chose a conventional name for the baby.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给宝宝取了个传统的名字。
senses.why: A well-worn path is easy to walk, and easy to notice.
senses.whyCN: 走熟的路好走，也容易被人看见。

senses.title: Usual in method
senses.definition: standard rather than special or new
senses.definitionCN: 采取标准做法而非特殊或新颖的做法
senses.example: The farm uses conventional tools.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场使用常规工具。
senses.why: Most work is done with what has already been tested.
senses.whyCN: 多数活儿是用已经验过的东西干的。

senses.title: Lacking surprise
senses.definition: plain and not unusual, sometimes in a dull way
senses.definitionCN: 普通、毫不特别，有时显得乏味
senses.example: The ending was too conventional to remember.
senses.exampleCN: 这个结尾太落套，让人记不住。
senses.why: A picture that copies every other picture leaves no mark.
senses.whyCN: 一张照抄其他画的画，不会留下痕迹。

intro.en: Conventional is convention plus the adjective ending -al, from Latin convenire, to come together and agree.
intro.cn: conventional 是 convention 加形容词词尾 -al 构成，源头是拉丁语 convenire（走到一起并取得一致）。

items.en: Convenire meant to meet and to agree.
items.cn: convenire 意为会面并取得一致。

items.en: Conventio named the agreement that followed a meeting.
items.cn: conventio 指会面之后达成的约定。

items.en: French convention carried the sense of an accepted custom.
items.cn: 法语 convention 带有被接受的习俗之义。

items.en: English convention meant a settled habit of a group.
items.cn: 英语 convention 指群体固定的习惯。

items.en: The adjective conventional grew to mean following that habit.
items.cn: 形容词 conventional 逐渐指依照这种习惯。

items.en: It now also hints at a lack of freshness.
items.cn: 如今它也暗示缺少新意。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin coming base ven-, and the meaning group names other words for what follows the usual path.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的来词基 ven-，近义组列出其他表示循常规的词。

in the accepted way
not following the usual way
following older customs
normal and not special

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a well-worn path, then move to tested tools and to a picture that copies every other picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从走熟的路开始，再到验过的工具，最后到照抄别的画的那幅画。

normal.en: Conventional is the adjective of convention: it follows the accepted way.
normal.cn: conventional 是 convention 的形容词：它照着被接受的方式走。

normal.en: A row of identical windows is convention in stone.
normal.cn: 一排一模一样的窗子，是石头做成的惯例。

normal.en: Conventional wisdom is what everyone says before thinking.
normal.cn: 传统看法是大家还没想就都会说的话。

normal.en: The word can praise safety or blame dullness.
normal.cn: 这个词既能夸稳妥，也能怪乏味。

normal.en: Same path, same steps, same result.
normal.cn: 同一条路，同样的步子，同样的结果。

abstract.en: Picture ten houses with the same white front.
abstract.cn: 想象十座房子有着同样的白色门面。

abstract.en: Picture a row of tools worn smooth by years.
abstract.cn: 想象一排被岁月磨得光滑的工具。

abstract.en: Picture a painting copied line for line from another.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅画逐线照抄了另一幅。

examples.en: She prefers conventional clothes at work.
examples.cn: 上班时她更喜欢传统样式的衣服。

examples.en: The farmers still use conventional methods.
examples.cn: 这些农民仍使用常规方法。

examples.en: His solution was clever but conventional.
examples.cn: 他的办法聪明却很落套。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conventional 记成 convention（惯例）加 al（形容词尾）：凡事照着惯例走，就是传统的、常规的。

root: 由 convention（惯例、约定）加形容词词尾 -al 构成，源头是拉丁语 convenire（走到一起并取得一致），指循惯例、合常规与缺少新意。

sensesIntro.en: From walking a well-worn path, to using tested tools, and at last to copying a picture already seen.
sensesIntro.cn: 从走一条熟路，到使用验过的工具，最后到照抄一幅已经看过的画。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ten houses sharing one white front.
core.cn: 核心意象：十座房子共用一个白色门面。

branches.en: The first sense simply follows what people accept.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只是照着人们接受的做法。

branches.en: The second sense chooses the standard tool.
branches.cn: 第二个义项选用标准的工具。

branches.en: The third sense notices what the habit costs.
branches.cn: 第三个义项看出这种习惯付出的代价。

branches.en: Custom and standard method are close neighbours.
branches.cn: 习俗与标准方法是一对近邻。

branches.en: A tested way can also become a dull one.
branches.cn: 验过的路，也可能变成乏味的路。

intro.en: Conventional is convention plus the adjective ending -al.

definition_en: an informal talk between people, or a serious discussion of a subject
core_image: 两人隔桌而坐，话语像球一样来回抛，始终不落地
scene: 咖啡馆里，两个人从天气聊到童年，一小时很快过去。Their conversation lasted until the shop closed.
sceneCN: 这里 conversation 指「交谈」（第 1 个义项：人们之间轻松的谈话）；句意是他们的交谈一直持续到店铺关门。

senses.title: An informal talk
senses.definition: a relaxed talk between two or more people
senses.definitionCN: 两人或多人之间轻松的谈话
senses.example: We had a long conversation about school.
senses.exampleCN: 我们聊了很久学校的事。
senses.why: Two voices taking turns is the oldest way to share a day.
senses.whyCN: 两个声音轮流开口，是分享一天最古老的方式。

senses.title: A serious discussion
senses.definition: a formal discussion of a subject between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体之间就某话题进行的正式讨论
senses.example: The two sides held a conversation on trade.
senses.exampleCN: 双方就贸易问题举行了会谈。
senses.why: When the stakes are high, a talk puts on a formal coat.
senses.whyCN: 事关重大时，谈话就披上了一件正式的外衣。

senses.title: The exchange itself
senses.definition: the act of talking together rather than any single remark
senses.definitionCN: 指一起谈话这一行为，而非某一句单独的话
senses.example: Conversation is how children learn their first words.
senses.exampleCN: 会话是孩子学会最初词汇的方式。
senses.why: A single line is a stone; a conversation is the river.
senses.whyCN: 一句话是一块石头，一次会话是一条河。

intro.en: Conversation comes from Latin conversari, to live or keep company with, built from com-, together, and versare, to turn.
intro.cn: conversation 来自拉丁语 conversari（与人相处、往来），由 com-（一起）与 versare（转动）构成。

items.en: Versare meant to turn something again and again.
items.cn: versare 意为把某物反复转动。

items.en: Conversari meant to live among people and spend time with them.
items.cn: conversari 意为在人群中生活、与人相处。

items.en: Conversatio named a way of life and daily dealings with others.
items.cn: conversatio 指生活方式以及与人的日常往来。

items.en: Old French conversation named a familiar talk between people.
items.cn: 古法语 conversation 指人与人之间的熟络谈话。

items.en: English conversation first meant living or dealing with people.
items.cn: 英语 conversation 最初指与人共同生活或往来。

items.en: Today it means a talk, usually friendly and unhurried.
items.cn: 今天它指一场谈话，通常友好而不慌不忙。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin turning base vers-, and the meaning group names other kinds of talk.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的转动词基 vers-，近义组列出其他表示谈话的说法。

entries.definition: to talk with another person
connected with talk between people
familiar with a subject
a friendly exchange of words
a light and informal talk
a conversation between two sides

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two voices taking turns, then move to a formal talk between groups and to conversation as a habit of living.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个声音轮流开口开始，再到团体之间的正式会谈，最后到作为一种生活习性的会话。

normal.en: Con- is together and vers is to turn, so a conversation is words turning between two people.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，vers 是转，conversation 就是在两人之间转来转去的话。

normal.en: One mouth alone is a speech; two mouths taking turns make a conversation.
normal.cn: 一张嘴独白是演讲，两张嘴轮流说才是交谈。

normal.en: The word looks like con plus version, as if each answer is a new version of the last.
normal.cn: 这个词看起来像 con 加 version，仿佛每个回答都是对上一句的新版本。

normal.en: A good conversation leaves both people slightly changed.
normal.cn: 一场好的交谈会让两个人都微微改变。

normal.en: No script, no stage: just two chairs turned toward each other.
normal.cn: 没有剧本，没有舞台，只有两把朝向彼此的椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a ball of words thrown gently back and forth.
abstract.cn: 想象一团话语被轻轻来回抛接。

abstract.en: Picture two cups on a table and steam rising between them.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两只杯子，热气在两者之间升起。

abstract.en: Picture a river turning at every stone yet never stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河绕过每块石头，却从不停下。

examples.en: They fell into conversation at the bus stop.
examples.cn: 他们在公交站随意聊了起来。

examples.en: I overheard a conversation about the new teacher.
examples.cn: 我无意中听到一段关于新老师的谈话。

examples.en: She keeps a notebook of conversations worth remembering.
examples.cn: 她把值得记住的谈话记在一个本子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conversation 记成 con（一起）加 vers（转）加 ion（名词）：话在两人之间转来转去，就是交谈。

root: 源自拉丁语 conversari（与人相处、往来），由 com-（一起）与 versare（转动）构成，本指共同生活，后专指彼此交谈。

sensesIntro.en: From two voices taking turns, to a formal talk between groups, and at last to the whole habit of talking together.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两个声音轮流开口，到团体之间的正式会谈，最后到一起谈话这一整体习性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball of words thrown gently back and forth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团话语被轻轻来回抛接。

branches.en: A relaxed talk lets two people share an ordinary day.
branches.cn: 轻松的谈话让两个人分享平凡的一天。

branches.en: A formal talk carries weight and often has a purpose.
branches.cn: 正式的会谈有分量，通常带有目的。

branches.en: The habit of talking together is how a language is passed on.
branches.cn: 一起谈话的习性，正是语言得以传递的方式。

branches.en: Both are talk, differing only in tone and setting.
branches.cn: 两者都是谈话，只在语气与场合上不同。

branches.en: A single meeting and a lifelong habit both rest on exchange.
branches.cn: 一次会面与一生的习惯，都建立在交流之上。

intro.en: Conversation is built on Latin com-, together, plus versare, to turn, and the noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: conversation 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、versare（转动）与名词词尾 -ation 构成。

latinIntro.en: The turning base vers- also runs through convert, reverse and version.
latinIntro.cn: 转动词基 vers- 也贯穿 convert、reverse 与 version。

items.meaningCN: 在人与人之间来回转的谈话

items.example: He wrote in a conversational style.

items.meaningCN: 把某物转成另一种形态

items.exampleCN: 他们把谷仓改成了工作室。

items.meaning: to turn something the other way

items.meaning: a form turned out from an original
items.meaningCN: 由原作转出的一种形态

definition_zh: 转变；转换；换算；使改变信仰；皈依者
definition_en: to change something into another form or use, or a person who has adopted a new belief
core_image: 一只旧木箱被拆开，重新钉成一张书桌
scene: 老仓库空了许多年，如今门口挂上了书店的牌子。They plan to convert the warehouse into a bookstore.
sceneCN: 这里 convert 指「改造；转变」（第 1 个义项：把某物改成另一种形态或用途）；句意是他们打算把仓库改造成书店。

senses.title: To change form or use
senses.definition: to change something so that it takes a different form or serves a new purpose
senses.definitionCN: 改变某物，使其呈现另一种形态或有了新用途
senses.example: The barn was converted into a house.
senses.exampleCN: 这座谷仓被改造成了住宅。
senses.why: The same material can serve twice if the shape is changed.
senses.whyCN: 同样的材料，只要改变形状，就能再用一次。

senses.title: To change units or money
senses.definition: to change a value from one system or currency into another
senses.definitionCN: 把数值从一种体系或货币换成另一种
senses.example: You can convert pounds into dollars here.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以在这里把英镑换成美元。
senses.why: Two languages of counting need a bridge, and this verb is that bridge.
senses.whyCN: 两套计数语言之间需要桥，这个动词就是那座桥。

senses.title: A person who has changed belief
senses.definition: someone who has adopted a new religion or set of ideas
senses.definitionCN: 接受了新宗教或新观念的人
senses.example: He became a convert to the new method.
senses.exampleCN: 他转而拥护这种新方法。
senses.why: When a view turns a person around, the person is named after the turn.
senses.whyCN: 当一种看法把一个人转了个方向，人就用这次转向来命名。

intro.en: Convert comes from Latin convertere, to turn about, built from com-, together, and vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: convert 来自拉丁语 convertere（转过来），由 com-（一起）与 vertere（转）构成。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, twist or change direction.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动、扭动或改变方向。

items.en: Convertere meant to turn something right round or turn it into another thing.
items.cn: convertere 意为把某物整个转过来，或把它变成另一样东西。

items.en: Conversus, the turned one, described a person or thing changed completely.
items.cn: conversus 指被转过来的人或物，形容彻底改变。

items.en: Old French convertir kept both the physical and the religious senses.
items.cn: 古法语 convertir 同时保留了物理与宗教两种含义。

items.en: English convert first meant to turn from one belief to another.
items.cn: 英语 convert 最初指从一种信仰转向另一种。

items.en: The word now also covers files, fuel and currency.
items.cn: 今天这个词也涵盖文件、燃料与货币的转换。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin turning base vert-, and the meaning group names other verbs of change.

normal.en: Con- is together and vert is to turn, so convert is to turn a thing into a new shape.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，vert 是转，convert 就是把东西转成一个新样子。

normal.en: Same wood, new table: nothing is lost, only rearranged.
normal.cn: 同样的木头，新的桌子：什么也没少，只是重新排列。

normal.en: A file becomes a picture, a pound becomes a dollar, a sum becomes a score.
normal.cn: 文件变成图片，英镑变成美元，算式变成得分。

normal.en: The noun convert is a person who has made this turn in belief.
normal.cn: 名词 convert 就是在信仰上完成这次转向的人。

normal.en: Remember the stress moves: con-VERT the verb, CON-vert the person.
normal.cn: 记住重音会移动：动词读 con-VERT，指人时读 CON-vert。

abstract.en: Picture a key melted down and recast as a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙被熔化，重新铸成戒指。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows curving into one circle.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭头弯成一个圆。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp turned from a dark corner to a bright wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯从暗角转向明亮的墙面。

examples.en: They converted the old factory into flats.
examples.cn: 他们把旧工厂改成了公寓。

examples.en: The app can convert your photos into a short film.
examples.cn: 这个应用能把你的照片转成一段短片。

examples.en: He is a recent convert to cycling.
examples.cn: 他最近成了骑行爱好者。

sensesIntro.en: From a thing turned into a new shape, to values exchanged, and at last to a person turned toward a new belief.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一件东西被转成新形态，到数值互换，最后到一个人转向新的信仰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old box taken apart and nailed into a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只旧箱子被拆开，钉成一张书桌。

branches.en: A building or object is turned to a new purpose.
branches.cn: 一座建筑或一件物品被转向新的用途。

branches.en: A number or a note changes system without losing worth.
branches.cn: 一个数字或一张钞票换了体系，却不失价值。

branches.en: A person turns, and the turn gives the person a new name.
branches.cn: 一个人转了向，这次转向就给了他一个新的称呼。

branches.en: Both are conversions of form, one physical and one abstract.
branches.cn: 两者都是形态转换，一个具体，一个抽象。

branches.en: Money and belief both change hands and change sides.
branches.cn: 金钱与信仰都会换手，也会换边。

intro.en: Convert is built on Latin com-, together, plus vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: convert 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 vertere（转）构成。

latinIntro.en: The turning base vert- also runs through reverse, version and versatile.
latinIntro.cn: 转动词基 vert- 也贯穿 reverse、version 与 versatile。

items.meaning: a device that changes one form into another
items.meaningCN: 把一种形态变成另一种的装置
items.exampleCN: 转换器发出轻微的嗡声。

items.meaning: to turn back the other way
a form produced from an original
items.meaningCN: 由原本产生的一种形态

items.meaning: able to turn to many tasks

definition_en: a court decision that someone is guilty, or a strong and steady belief
core_image: 一纸判决放在桌上，胸口另有一只手始终不肯松开
scene: 宣判之后，她仍抬起头，说自己相信这条路是对的。She spoke with the conviction of someone who had waited years.
sceneCN: 这里 conviction 指「坚定信念」（第 2 个义项：深信不疑的看法）；句意是她说话时带着一种等了多年的坚定信念。

senses.title: A court ruling of guilt
senses.definition: an official decision that a person is guilty of a crime
senses.definitionCN: 正式认定某人犯有某项罪行的决定
senses.example: The conviction was overturned on appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 这项定罪在上诉时被推翻了。
senses.why: A single ruling can follow a person for the rest of a life.
senses.whyCN: 一次裁决可能跟着一个人走过余生。

senses.title: A steady belief
senses.definition: a firm belief that something is true or right
senses.definitionCN: 坚信某事为真或为对的看法
senses.example: She lives by the conviction that work should be fair.
senses.exampleCN: 她秉持工作应当公平的信念生活。
senses.why: A belief that survives argument is held by something stronger than habit.
senses.whyCN: 经得住争辩的信念，靠的比习惯更结实。

intro.en: Conviction comes from Latin convictio, a proving of guilt, from convincere, to overcome with proof, built from com-, together, and vincere, to conquer.
intro.cn: conviction 来自拉丁语 convictio（证明有罪），源于 convincere（用证据驳倒），由 com-（一起）与 vincere（征服）构成。

items.en: Vincere meant to conquer and to carry the day.
items.cn: vincere 意为征服、占上风。

items.en: Convincere meant to overcome a person by clear proof.
items.cn: convincere 意为用清楚的证据把人驳倒。

items.en: Convictio named both the proof and the state of being proven wrong.
items.cn: convictio 既指证据，也指被证明有错的状态。

items.en: English conviction first meant the proving of guilt.
items.cn: 英语 conviction 最初指对罪行的证明。

items.en: The same word came to mean a belief held beyond doubt.
items.cn: 同一个词开始表示不容怀疑的信念。

items.en: Law keeps the first sense, while daily speech keeps the second.
items.cn: 法律保留了第一个义项，日常口语保留了第二个。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin conquering base vict-, and the meaning group names other words for belief and for legal decisions.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的征服词基 vict-，近义组列出其他表示信念与法律裁决的词。

entries.definition: to find someone guilty in court
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上判定某人有罪

entries.definition: to make someone feel sure
the act of forcing someone out of a place
a feeling that something is true
a state of being completely sure
the punishment given by a court

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a verdict written down, then move to a belief that cannot be argued away.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一纸写下的判决开始，再到一个争辩不掉的信念。

normal.en: Convict is the act and conviction is the result, so a conviction is what is left after proof has won.
normal.cn: convict 是动作，conviction 是结果：证据赢了之后留下的东西就是定罪。

normal.en: The same word serves the courtroom and the heart.
normal.cn: 同一个词，既服务法庭，也服务人心。

normal.en: Say it with conviction and people lean in; say it without and they look away.
normal.cn: 带着信念说，人会靠近；不带信念说，人会转开目光。

normal.en: -ion turns the verb into a thing you can carry.
normal.cn: -ion 把动词变成一件可以带在身上的东西。

normal.en: A previous conviction is a past that keeps speaking in court.
normal.cn: 前科是一段在法庭上不断开口的过去。

abstract.en: Picture a stamped paper lying beside a closed hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张盖了章的纸，旁边是一只攥紧的手。

abstract.en: Picture a candle that stays lit in a windy room.
abstract.cn: 想象一支在风里也不灭的蜡烛。

abstract.en: Picture a root gripping stone and refusing to let go.
abstract.cn: 想象一条根抓住石头，怎么也不松开。

examples.en: He has two previous convictions for theft.
examples.cn: 他有两项盗窃前科。

examples.en: She argued her case with quiet conviction.
examples.cn: 她以平静而坚定的信念为自己的主张辩护。

examples.en: It is my conviction that small steps change a town.
examples.cn: 我深信小小的步伐能改变一座城镇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conviction 记成 convict（定罪）加 ion：法庭定下的罪，是定罪；心里定下的看法，是信念。

root: 源自拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒）的名词 convictio，由 com-（完全）与 vincere（征服）构成，本指证明有罪，后引申为坚定的信念。

sensesIntro.en: From a guilt proven in court, to a belief that proof cannot shake.
sensesIntro.cn: 从法庭上被证明的罪，到证据也摇不动的信念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a verdict sheet beside a tightly closed hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张判决书旁边，是一只攥紧的手。

branches.en: A court writes down what it has proved.
branches.cn: 法庭把已经证明的事写下来。

branches.en: A person holds fast to what argument cannot move.
branches.cn: 一个人紧紧抓住争辩也动不了的东西。

branches.en: Both are things settled beyond easy doubt.
branches.cn: 两者都是不容轻易动摇的定论。

branches.en: The legal sense is public, written and dated.
branches.cn: 法律义项是公开的、书面的、有日期的。

branches.en: The personal sense is quiet, inward and unrecorded.
branches.cn: 个人义项是安静的、向内的、不被记录的。

intro.en: Conviction is convict plus -ion, resting on Latin convincere, to overcome with proof.
intro.cn: conviction 是 convict 加 -ion，根源是拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒）。

latinIntro.en: The conquering base vict- or vinc- also runs through convince, victory and invincible.
latinIntro.cn: 征服词基 vict- 或 vinc- 也贯穿 convince、victory 与 invincible。

items.meaningCN: 已经定下的裁决或信念

items.meaning: to win someone to a belief
items.meaningCN: 把某人争取到某种看法上

items.exampleCN: 那位冠军看起来不可战胜。

definition_en: to make someone believe that something is true, or to persuade someone to act
core_image: 一个人把一条清楚的路指给另一个人看，对方终于点头
scene: 她拿出一张张照片，父亲看完后不再反对。The photos convinced him that the plan was safe.
sceneCN: 这里 convince 指「使确信」（第 1 个义项：让某人相信某事为真）；句意是这些照片使他确信这个计划是安全的。

derivatives.zh: 有说服力的；令人信服的

senses.title: To make someone sure
senses.definition: to cause someone to believe that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 使某人相信某事为真
senses.example: The evidence convinced her that he was honest.
senses.exampleCN: 证据使她确信他是诚实的。
senses.why: Doubt is a door held shut, and proof is the hand that opens it.
senses.whyCN: 怀疑是一扇关着的门，证据就是推开它的那只手。

senses.title: To persuade into action
senses.definition: to talk someone into doing something
senses.definitionCN: 通过劝说使某人去做某事
senses.example: He convinced his parents to let him travel.
senses.exampleCN: 他说服父母让他去旅行。
senses.why: Belief is half the work; the other half is a step taken.
senses.whyCN: 相信只算一半，另一半是迈出那一步。

intro.en: Convince comes from Latin convincere, to overcome with proof, built from com-, together, and vincere, to conquer.
intro.cn: convince 来自拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒），由 com-（一起、完全）与 vincere（征服）构成。

items.en: Vincere meant to conquer an opponent in a struggle.
items.cn: vincere 意为在较量中战胜对手。

items.en: Convincere meant to defeat someone with reasons rather than force.
items.cn: convincere 意为用道理而非武力把人驳倒。

items.en: English convince first meant to prove a person wrong.
items.cn: 英语 convince 最初指证明某人有错。

items.en: The meaning softened to making someone feel certain.
items.cn: 词义变柔和，转为使某人感到确定。

items.en: A new pattern, convince someone to do, became common.
items.cn: convince someone to do 这一新搭配变得常见。

items.en: Today it covers both belief and action.
items.cn: 今天它同时涵盖相信与行动。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin conquering base vinc-, and the meaning group names other ways of bringing someone to a view.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的征服词基 vinc-，近义组列出其他使人接受看法的说法。

entries.definition: to find someone guilty in court
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上判定某人有罪

entries.definition: able to make people believe
too strong to be beaten
to make someone agree to do something
to tell someone firmly so doubt goes away
entries.definitionCN: 坚定地告诉某人以消除疑虑

entries.definition: to give someone enough reason to accept
entries.definitionCN: 给某人足够的理由接受

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with proof winning a mind, then move to a person moving from doubt to a decision.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从证据赢下一个头脑开始，再到一个人从怀疑走向决定。

normal.en: Con- is completely and vince is to conquer, so convince is to conquer doubt completely.
normal.cn: con- 是完全，vince 是征服，convince 就是把怀疑彻底征服。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with convict: one changes a mind, the other closes a door.
normal.cn: 别和 convict 搞混：一个改变想法，一个关上牢门。

normal.en: You convince a friend; you convict a defendant.
normal.cn: 你说服朋友；你给被告定罪。

normal.en: The adjective convincing adds -ing, as if the argument is still working on you.
normal.cn: 形容词 convincing 加了 -ing，仿佛那套论证还在你身上起作用。

normal.en: A convinced person walks differently from a merely informed one.
normal.cn: 确信的人走路的姿态，和仅仅被告知的人不一样。

abstract.en: Picture a locked gate opening after a key turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙转动后，锁着的门开了。

abstract.en: Picture a scale slowly settling on one side.
abstract.cn: 想象天平慢慢落向一边。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing down a clear road at dusk.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏里一只手指出一条清楚的路。

examples.en: Nothing you say will convince me otherwise.
examples.cn: 你说什么也无法使我相信别的。

examples.en: She convinced the class to join the clean-up.
examples.cn: 她说服全班参加清洁活动。

examples.en: His explanation was simple and convincing.
examples.cn: 他的解释简单而有说服力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 convince 记成 con（完全）加 vince（征服）：把对方的怀疑完全征服，就是使确信、说服。

root: 源自拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒），由 com-（完全）与 vincere（征服）构成，本指以理服人，后指使确信与说服。

sensesIntro.en: From proof winning a mind, to a mind deciding to move.
sensesIntro.cn: 从证据赢下一个头脑，到这个头脑决定行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pointing down a clear road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手指出一条清楚的路。

branches.en: Evidence settles the question of what is true.
branches.cn: 证据解决了什么为真这个问题。

branches.en: A settled mind then agrees to act.
branches.cn: 安定的心随后同意行动。

branches.en: Belief and action are two halves of one movement.
branches.cn: 相信与行动是同一个动作的两半。

branches.en: The first sense is about truth and evidence.
branches.cn: 第一个义项关乎真相与证据。

branches.en: The second is about will and permission.
branches.cn: 第二个义项关乎意愿与许可。

intro.en: Convince is built on Latin com-, completely, plus vincere, to conquer.
intro.cn: convince 由拉丁语 com-（完全）与 vincere（征服）构成。

latinIntro.en: The conquering base vinc- also runs through convict, victory and invincible.
latinIntro.cn: 征服词基 vinc- 也贯穿 convict、victory 与 invincible。

items.exampleCN: 随后是一场令人信服的胜利。

items.meaning: the gaining of the upper hand

items.exampleCN: 他们觉得自己不可战胜。

items.meaning: to put a person out by force

definition_en: to prepare food with heat, a person who prepares food, or to change records dishonestly
core_image: 灶上锅盖掀起，白汽带着香味散满整个厨房
scene: 放学回家，锅里的汤正咕嘟作响。My father is cooking dinner in the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 cook 指「烹饪」（第 1 个义项：用加热的方式做食物）；句意是我父亲正在厨房做晚饭。

senses.title: To prepare food with heat
senses.definition: to make food ready to eat by heating it
senses.definitionCN: 通过加热使食物可以食用
senses.example: She cooked rice for thirty people.
senses.exampleCN: 她为三十个人煮了米饭。
senses.why: Fire turns raw things into a meal and a house into a home.
senses.whyCN: 火把生的东西变成一餐饭，也把房子变成家。

senses.title: A person who prepares food
senses.definition: someone whose job is preparing meals
senses.definitionCN: 以做饭为职业的人
senses.example: The cook came out to greet us.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师走出来迎接我们。
senses.why: The act and the person share one short word in English.
senses.whyCN: 在英语里，这个动作和这个人共用一个短短的单词。

senses.title: To falsify records
senses.definition: to change numbers or accounts in order to cheat
senses.definitionCN: 为了作弊而改动数字或账目
senses.example: They were caught cooking the accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 他们篡改账目被抓住了。
senses.why: Bad numbers are like raw food: someone cooks them to make them look finished.
senses.whyCN: 假数字像生食材：有人把它煮过，好让它看起来已经做好。

intro.en: Cook comes from Old English coc, a cook, borrowed from Latin coquus, from coquere, to cook or ripen.
intro.cn: cook 来自古英语 coc（厨师），借自拉丁语 coquus，源于 coquere（煮、使成熟）。

items.en: Coquere meant to cook, boil or ripen food.
items.cn: coquere 意为煮、煮开或使食物成熟。

items.en: Coquus named the person who did this work.
items.cn: coquus 指做这项工作的人。

items.en: Old English coc meant a cook in a household.
items.cn: 古英语 coc 指家中的厨师。

items.en: The same word began to serve as a verb as well.
items.cn: 同一个词也开始当动词用。

items.en: Cooking became a common topic in printed household books.
items.cn: 烹饪成为印行家政书中的常见话题。

items.en: The slang sense of falsifying accounts appeared much later.
items.cn: 篡改账目的俚语义项出现得晚得多。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short cook- base, and the meaning group names other words for preparing food.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 cook- 词基，近义组列出其他表示做饭的词。

entries.definition: a machine or pot for cooking food
the skill of preparing food
a small sweet biscuit
a trained cook in a restaurant
entries.definitionCN: 餐馆里受过训练的厨师

entries.definition: to get food ready to be eaten
entries.definitionCN: 把食物准备好以供食用

entries.definition: to cook food in an oven

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a pot steaming on a stove, then move to the person at the stove and to numbers quietly altered.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从灶上冒汽的锅开始，再到灶边的人，最后到被悄悄改动的数字。

normal.en: Cook is a verb and a noun at once: the cook cooks.
normal.cn: cook 既是动词又是名词：厨师做饭。

normal.en: The word is as short as a quick stir of the spoon.
normal.cn: 这个词和快搅一下勺子一样短。

normal.en: Cook a meal for guests, and the house smells warm.
normal.cn: 给客人做一顿饭，屋里就有了暖味。

normal.en: Cook the books and the warmth turns to smoke.
normal.cn: 篡改账目，这股暖意就变成了烟。

normal.en: Remember the -er words: cooker is the stove, cookery is the skill.
normal.cn: 记住带 -er 的词：cooker 是炉灶，cookery 是技艺。

abstract.en: Picture steam lifting a lid and curling toward a window.
abstract.cn: 想象蒸汽顶起锅盖，卷向窗户。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon tasting soup in a bright kitchen.
abstract.cn: 想象明亮的厨房里，一把勺子尝着汤。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger with one figure written over another.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿上，一个数字盖住了另一个。

examples.en: He cooked noodles for the whole team.
examples.cn: 他给全队煮了面条。

examples.en: My grandmother is the best cook I know.
examples.cn: 我奶奶是我认识的最好的厨师。

examples.en: The manager was accused of cooking the figures.
examples.cn: 经理被指控篡改数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cook 记成一口锅的咕嘟声：锅一响，饭就熟了，做这件事的人也叫 cook。

root: 源自拉丁语 coquere（煮、使成熟），经 coquus（厨师）借入古英语作 coc，动词与名词同形，后引申出篡改账目的俚语义。

sensesIntro.en: From a pot of food over fire, to the person beside it, and at last to numbers cooked to hide the truth.
sensesIntro.cn: 从火上的一锅食物，到锅边的人，最后到被烹煮以掩盖真相的数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pot lid lifting with a cloud of steam.
core.cn: 核心意象：锅盖被一团蒸汽顶起。

branches.en: Heat changes raw food into a meal.
branches.cn: 加热把生食变成一餐饭。

branches.en: A person can be named by the work of the hands.
branches.cn: 一个人可以用双手的活计来称呼。

branches.en: False figures are prepared like food, to look ready.
branches.cn: 假数字像食物一样被加工，好显得已经做好。

branches.en: The act and its doer share one plain word.
branches.cn: 动作与做动作的人共用一个朴素的词。

branches.en: Both senses are about making something presentable.
branches.cn: 两个义项都关乎把东西弄得像样。

intro.en: Cook rests on Latin coquere, to cook or ripen, which reached English through Old English coc.
intro.cn: cook 源于拉丁语 coquere（煮、使成熟），经古英语 coc 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The cooking base coqu- also shows in cuisine, concoct and biscuit.
latinIntro.cn: 烹饪词基 coqu- 也出现在 cuisine、concoct 与 biscuit 中。

items.meaning: to cook up a mixture or a story
items.meaningCN: 把材料煮成一体，也指编造

definition_en: a device or pot used for cooking, or a fruit that is good for cooking
core_image: 厨房角落一台白色炉灶，四个灶眼像四只安静的圆眼
scene: 搬进新家那天，母亲第一件事是擦净厨房里的炉灶。She cleaned the cooker before unpacking the plates.
sceneCN: 这里 cooker 指「炉灶；炊具」（第 1 个义项：用来烹煮食物的器具）；句意是她先擦净炉灶，再拆开盘子。

collocations.phrase: put the pot on the cooker

senses.title: A device for cooking
senses.definition: a machine or large pot that is used to cook food
senses.definitionCN: 用来烹煮食物的机器或大锅
senses.example: The cooker has four rings and a small oven.
senses.exampleCN: 这台炉灶有四个灶眼和一个小烤箱。
senses.why: The tool takes the name of the act it exists to serve.
senses.whyCN: 工具借用了它生来要服务的那个动作的名字。

senses.title: A fruit for cooking
senses.definition: a fruit, especially an apple, grown to be cooked rather than eaten raw
senses.definitionCN: 专门用于烹煮而非生吃的水果，尤指苹果
senses.example: These cookers are too sour to eat raw.
senses.exampleCN: 这些煮食苹果太酸，不能生吃。
senses.why: Some fruit is grown for the pot, not for the hand.
senses.whyCN: 有些水果是为锅种的，不是为手种的。

intro.en: Cooker is cook plus the agent ending -er, which first named a person and later the machine.
intro.cn: cooker 是 cook 加施事词尾 -er，最初指人，后来指机器。

items.en: Coc named the person who prepared food.
items.cn: coc 指准备食物的人。

items.en: The verb coken described the work done at the fire.
items.cn: 动词 coken 描述在火边干的活。

items.en: Cooker first meant a person employed to cook.
items.cn: cooker 最初指受雇做饭的人。

items.en: With new kitchen machines, cooker shifted to the device itself.
items.cn: 随着厨房机器出现，cooker 转指器具本身。

items.en: Compounds like rice cooker and slow cooker are now common.
items.cn: rice cooker 与 slow cooker 之类的复合词如今很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short cook- base, and the meaning group names other kitchen words for heat and cooking.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 cook- 词基，近义组列出其他与加热和烹煮有关的厨房词。

entries.definition: to prepare food with heat
the skill of preparing food
a small sweet biscuit
a device with burners for cooking
a closed box for baking food
entries.definitionCN: 用来烘烤食物的封闭箱体

entries.definition: a large cooker with an oven

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a stove in a new kitchen, then move to fruit grown for the pot.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从新厨房里的一台炉灶开始，再到为锅而种的水果。

normal.en: Cook plus -er makes the thing that cooks, just as print plus -er makes the printer.
normal.cn: cook 加 -er 就是会煮东西的物件，正如 print 加 -er 是打印机。

normal.en: A cook is a person; a cooker is a machine.
normal.cn: cook 是人，cooker 是机器。

normal.en: In British homes the cooker is the whole stove, not just one pot.
normal.cn: 在英国家里，cooker 指整台炉灶，而不只是一口锅。

normal.en: Rice cooker and slow cooker show the word at work in compounds.
normal.cn: rice cooker 与 slow cooker 展示了这个词在复合词中的用法。

normal.en: A cooker apple is named for what will happen to it, not for how it tastes raw.
normal.cn: 煮食苹果是按它将要经历的事命名的，不是按生吃的味道。

abstract.en: Picture four round burners glowing in a dark kitchen.
abstract.cn: 想象暗厨房里四个圆形灶眼发着光。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy lid rattling on a pot.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的锅盖在锅上轻轻震动。

abstract.en: Picture a basket of sour apples beside a saucepan.
abstract.cn: 想象一篮酸苹果放在深锅旁边。

examples.en: She wiped the cooker after every meal.
examples.cn: 她每顿饭后都擦一遍炉灶。

examples.en: A rice cooker saves time on busy evenings.
examples.cn: 忙碌的晚上，电饭锅能省下时间。

examples.en: The old cooker gave off a smell of gas.
examples.cn: 那台旧炉灶散发出煤气味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cooker 记成 cook（煮）加 er（东西）：用来煮东西的物件，就是炉灶与炊具。

root: 由 cook（烹饪）加施事词尾 -er 构成，本指做饭的人，十九世纪起转指炉灶等炊事器具。

sensesIntro.en: From the person who cooks, to the machine that does the work, and to fruit meant for the pot.
sensesIntro.cn: 从做饭的人，到承担这项工作的机器，再到为锅而种的水果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white stove with four quiet burners.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台有四个安静灶眼的白色炉灶。

branches.en: A machine holds the heat that cooks the meal.
branches.cn: 机器承住热量，把饭煮熟。

branches.en: A fruit is chosen for the pot rather than the plate.
branches.cn: 一种水果被选中进锅，而不是上盘生吃。

branches.en: Both senses tie an object to the act of cooking.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把某样东西系在烹煮这个动作上。

branches.en: The device sense grew from the older word for a person.
branches.cn: 器具义项是从更早指人的词义长出来的。

branches.en: The fruit sense is local and survives mainly in British speech.
branches.cn: 水果义项较地方化，主要保留在英式说法里。

intro.en: Cooker is cook plus -er, the old ending for a person or thing that does an action.
intro.cn: cooker 是 cook 加 -er，这个古老词尾表示做某动作的人或物。

latinIntro.en: The cooking base coqu- also shows in cuisine, concoct and biscuit.
latinIntro.cn: 烹饪词基 coqu- 也出现在 cuisine、concoct 与 biscuit 中。

definition_zh: 曲奇饼干；网络小甜饼；强悍的人
definition_en: a small sweet biscuit, a small file a website stores on your computer, or a tough person
core_image: 烤箱门一开，一盘圆圆的小饼冒着热气
scene: 她端出刚烤好的圆饼，孩子们伸手就抓。The children finished every cookie on the plate.
sceneCN: 这里 cookie 指「曲奇饼干」（第 1 个义项：小块的甜饼）；句意是孩子们把盘子里的饼干都吃完了。

pos.zh: 网络小甜饼；网站存下的数据文件

derivatives.zh: 千篇一律的；按模子做的

senses.title: A small sweet biscuit
senses.definition: a small flat cake baked until crisp and sweet
senses.definitionCN: 烤得酥脆香甜的小块扁饼
senses.example: She left a plate of cookies on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她在桌上留了一盘饼干。
senses.why: A small round thing can carry more warmth than a whole meal.
senses.whyCN: 一块圆圆的小东西，能比一整餐饭更暖人心。

senses.title: A file stored by a website
senses.definition: a small piece of data a website keeps on a visitor's computer
senses.definitionCN: 网站留在访客电脑上的一小段数据
senses.example: The site uses a cookie to remember your name.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网站用一段小数据记住你的名字。
senses.why: The sweet name hides a small memory kept for the next visit.
senses.whyCN: 这个甜甜的名字背后，是一份留给下次来访的小记忆。

senses.title: A tough person
senses.definition: a person who is strong and not easily upset or beaten
senses.definitionCN: 强悍而不会轻易受挫或被打败的人
senses.example: She is one tough cookie in a debate.
senses.exampleCN: 她在辩论中是个很难对付的人。
senses.why: In slang, a hard biscuit becomes a hard person.
senses.whyCN: 在俚语里，硬邦邦的饼干变成了硬邦邦的人。

intro.en: Cookie comes from Dutch koekje, a little cake, the diminutive of koek, cake.
intro.cn: cookie 来自荷兰语 koekje（小饼），是 koek（饼）的指小形式。

items.en: Koek meant a flat baked cake.
items.cn: koek 意为烤成的扁饼。

items.en: Koekje was the small, affectionate form of koek.
items.cn: koekje 是 koek 的指小形式，带有亲切意味。

items.en: Dutch settlers brought the word into American English.
items.cn: 荷兰移民把这个词带进了美国英语。

items.en: Cookie settled as the everyday word, beside British biscuit.
items.cn: cookie 成为美式日常用词，与英式 biscuit 并存。

items.en: The computing sense appeared in the late twentieth century.
items.cn: 计算机领域的义项在二十世纪后期出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short cook- base, and the meaning group names other baked sweet foods.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 cook- 词基，近义组列出其他烘烤的甜食。
