normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a warm tray of biscuits, then move to a hidden file and to a hard person.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一盘温热的饼干开始，再到一个藏起来的文件，最后到一个强硬的人。

normal.en: Cookie looks like cook plus ie, a little thing that has been cooked.
normal.cn: cookie 看起来像 cook 加 ie，就是被烤过的小东西。

normal.en: The Dutch gave the word its soft k sound and its small ending.
normal.cn: 荷兰语给了这个词柔和的 k 音和指小的词尾。

normal.en: A website cookie is also a small thing kept for later.
normal.cn: 网站的小甜饼也是一样留到以后用的小东西。

normal.en: A tough cookie is not sweet at all in an argument.
normal.cn: 在争论里，a tough cookie 一点也不甜。

normal.en: Think of a cookie jar that never stays full for long.
normal.cn: 想想那只从来满不了太久的饼干罐。

abstract.en: Picture a tray of round biscuits cooling by a window.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘圆饼干在窗边晾凉。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny note slipped into a drawer for next time.
abstract.cn: 想象一张小纸条被塞进抽屉，留给下次。

abstract.en: Picture a hard shell around a soft centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一层硬壳包着柔软的内里。

examples.en: We baked a batch of cookies for the guests.
examples.cn: 我们为客人烤了一批饼干。

examples.en: This website asks you to accept its cookies.
examples.cn: 这个网站要求你接受它的小甜饼文件。

examples.en: The old coach is a tough cookie.
examples.cn: 那位老教练是个很硬气的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cookie 记成 cook（烤）加 ie（小东西）：烤出来的小东西，就是小甜饼。

root: 源自荷兰语 koekje（小饼），是 koek（饼）的指小形式，随荷兰移民进入美式英语，后又引申出网络数据文件与强悍之人等义。

sensesIntro.en: From a small baked cake, to a small file kept by a website, and at last to a person hard to break.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一块烤成的小饼，到网站存下的小文件，最后到难以击垮的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm tray of round biscuits.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盘温热的圆饼干。

branches.en: A small sweet cake is baked crisp.
branches.cn: 一块小甜饼被烤得酥脆。

branches.en: A tiny file remembers a visitor between visits.
branches.cn: 一个小文件在两次来访之间记住访客。

branches.en: Slang turns a hard biscuit into a hard person.
branches.cn: 俚语把硬饼干变成了硬气的人。

branches.en: Both are small, handy things kept for later.
branches.cn: 两者都是留着以后用的小而方便的东西。

branches.en: Both uses were born in everyday American speech.
branches.cn: 两种用法都诞生于美国日常口语。

intro.en: Cookie is a Dutch loanword built on koek, cake, with the small ending -je.
intro.cn: cookie 是荷兰语借词，由 koek（饼）加指小词尾 -je 构成。

latinIntro.en: The cooking base coqu- also shows in cuisine, concoct and biscuit.
latinIntro.cn: 烹饪词基 coqu- 也出现在 cuisine、concoct 与 biscuit 中。

definition_zh: 凉爽的；冷静的；酷的；使变凉
definition_en: slightly cold, calm and controlled, fashionable, or to make something less warm
core_image: 夏夜的风穿过窗纱，桌上水杯的外壁凝出细水珠
scene: 争执到最响的时候，他只是把声音放低。Try to stay cool when everyone else is shouting.
sceneCN: 这里 cool 指「冷静的」（第 2 个义项：镇静而不被情绪带走）；句意是当别人都在大喊时，尽量保持冷静。

senses.title: Slightly cold
senses.definition: pleasantly low in temperature, not cold enough to hurt
senses.definitionCN: 温度宜人偏低，尚未冷到难受
senses.example: A cool wind came off the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 湖面上吹来一阵凉风。
senses.why: The body sighs with relief when heat steps back a little.
senses.whyCN: 热气稍稍退开，身体就松了一口气。

senses.title: Calm under pressure
senses.definition: not excited, angry or frightened in a difficult moment
senses.definitionCN: 在困难时刻不激动、不发怒、不惊慌
senses.example: She stayed cool while the others argued.
senses.exampleCN: 别人争吵时她保持冷静。
senses.why: A cool head is a warm heart kept under control.
senses.whyCN: 冷静的头脑，是被管住的热心肠。

senses.title: Fashionable and admired
senses.definition: very fashionable, impressive or approved of by others
senses.definitionCN: 非常时髦、令人印象深刻或被人认可的
senses.example: That old bike is still cool.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧自行车还是很酷。
senses.why: What is admired keeps a distance, and distance feels cool.
senses.whyCN: 被欣赏的东西总保持一点距离，而距离感就是凉意。

intro.en: Cool comes from Old English col, cold, from a Germanic root shared with cold itself.
intro.cn: cool 来自古英语 col（冷的），词根与 cold 同属日耳曼语族。

items.en: A root meaning cold lay behind words in several northern languages.
items.cn: 一个意为冷的词根藏在几种北方语言里。

items.en: Col meant moderately cold, milder than cold.
items.cn: col 意为适度地冷，比 cold 温和。

items.en: The word extended from air to drink and to temper.
items.cn: 这个词从空气扩展到饮料，再扩展到脾气。

items.en: Cool gained the sense of calm and self-controlled.
items.cn: cool 获得了冷静、自制的含义。

items.en: Jazz and youth culture gave it the sense of stylish.
items.cn: 爵士乐与青年文化赋予它时髦的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the same cool base, and the meaning group names nearby ideas of cold and calm.
note.cn: 形近组由同一个 cool 词基构成，近义组列出与冷和冷静相近的说法。

entries.definition: a box or device that keeps things cold
entries.definitionCN: 让东西保持低温的箱子或装置

entries.definition: in a calm or unfriendly way
the state of being cool
uncomfortably cold
peaceful and not excited
following the style of the moment

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a breeze on a warm evening, then move to a head that keeps its balance and to a style others copy.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从暖夜里的微风开始，再到一颗保持平衡的脑袋，最后到别人模仿的风格。

normal.en: One short word covers temperature, temper and taste.
normal.cn: 一个短短的单词，同时管温度、脾气和品味。

normal.en: Cool weather cools a drink, and a cool head cools a quarrel.
normal.cn: 凉爽的天气让饮料变凉，冷静的头脑让争吵降温。

normal.en: Compare cool with cold: cool is the pleasant side of cold.
normal.cn: 把 cool 和 cold 比一比：cool 是冷里让人舒服的那一面。

normal.en: To play it cool is to keep the face calm while the heart races.
normal.cn: play it cool 就是心里乱跳，脸上却平静。

normal.en: The adjective and the verb share one shape, so the wind cools the room.
normal.cn: 形容词与动词同形，于是风把房间吹凉。

abstract.en: Picture a glass sweating on a table in July.
abstract.cn: 想象七月里桌上一只冒水珠的杯子。

abstract.en: Picture a lake surface with no ripple at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时没有一丝波纹的湖面。

abstract.en: Picture someone leaning back while others lean in.
abstract.cn: 想象别人都向前倾时，有个人向后靠着。

examples.en: The evening air turned cool after the rain.
examples.cn: 雨后傍晚的空气变凉了。

examples.en: He kept cool and answered every question slowly.
examples.cn: 他保持冷静，慢慢回答了每个问题。

examples.en: Let the soup cool before you taste it.
examples.cn: 让汤凉一点再尝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cool 记成一口凉气：温度退一步是凉爽，情绪退一步是冷静，风格退一步就成了酷。

root: 源自日耳曼语中意为冷的词根，古英语作 col，本指适度寒冷，后引申为冷静自制，二十世纪又引申为时髦。

sensesIntro.en: From air that is pleasantly cold, to a temper held steady, and at last to a style others admire.
sensesIntro.cn: 从宜人微凉的空气，到稳稳管住的脾气，最后到别人欣赏的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cool breeze moving through a warm room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一阵凉风穿过温热的房间。

branches.en: A lower temperature brings comfort.
branches.cn: 更低的温度带来舒适。

branches.en: A steady mind keeps its balance in noise.
branches.cn: 沉稳的心在喧闹里保持平衡。

branches.en: Admired style borrows the word for pleasant distance.
branches.cn: 被人欣赏的风格，借用了这种舒服的距离感。

branches.en: Both rest on a step back from heat.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在从热里退后一步。

branches.en: Calm and cool style both look unbothered.
branches.cn: 冷静与酷的风格，看起来都不慌不忙。

intro.en: Cool is a native Germanic word, and its family grows with -er, -ly, -ness and -ing.
intro.cn: cool 是本族日耳曼词，它的家族由 -er、-ly、-ness 与 -ing 扩展而来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base for cold, frig-, appears in fridge, frigid and refrigerant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示冷的词基 frig- 出现在 fridge、frigid 与 refrigerant 中。

items.meaning: a container that keeps things cold
items.meaningCN: 让东西保持低温的容器
items.example: Put the milk in the cooler.

items.meaning: the act of making less warm
a fluid that carries heat away

items.exampleCN: 这首歌如今听起来不酷了。

items.example: A cool-headed driver avoided the crash.
items.exampleCN: 一位冷静的司机避免了一场撞车。

definition_zh: 合作；为共同目标一起行动，也指愿意配合他人的态度
definition_en: the act of working together toward a shared goal, or the willingness to help when asked
core_image: 两个人各抬一端，把同一件重物搬到同一处
scene: 实验室里，两名研究人员一人扶住支架、一人拧紧螺丝，几分钟就把装置装好。One researcher steadies the frame while the other tightens the bolts, and the job is finished through cooperation.
sceneCN: 这里 cooperation 指「为共同目标一起行动」（第 1 个义项：各方分担同一任务的不同部分）；句意为一名研究者扶住支架、另一名拧紧螺丝，装置靠合作很快装好。图中可辨识物件：支架、螺丝、两只手、装配好的装置。

pos.zh: 合作；协作；配合（不可数；具体合作项目可用复数）

senses.title: Working together toward one goal
senses.definition: the act of working with others toward a shared aim
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起为共同目标做事
senses.example: One researcher steadies the frame while the other tightens the bolts.
senses.exampleCN: 一名研究者扶住支架，另一名拧紧螺丝。
senses.why: co- 'together' plus operari 'to work' says exactly what the word does: two or more agents put their work into one result.
senses.whyCN: co-「一起」加 operari「做事」，正好说出这个词的动作：两个或更多行动者把自己的劳动放进同一个结果。

senses.title: Willingness to help when asked
senses.definition: the readiness to assist someone who asks for help or permission
senses.definitionCN: 愿意帮助提出请求或需要许可的人
senses.example: Thank you for your cooperation during the inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 感谢您在检查期间的配合。
senses.why: the same word names the attitude behind joint work; a request for cooperation asks for access and effort rather than a formal partnership.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也指共同做事背后的态度；请求 cooperation 要的是配合与便利，而不是正式合伙关系。

senses.title: Mutual aid in nature
senses.definition: behavior in which organisms act together in ways that benefit both partners
senses.definitionCN: 生物共同行动、双方都获益的行为
senses.example: Ants and acacia trees cooperate: shelter for defence.
senses.exampleCN: 蚂蚁与金合欢合作：住所换防卫。
senses.why: biology borrowed the word because two species can also divide a job, and the shared benefit is measurable in survival and offspring.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了这个词，因为两个物种也能分担同一件事，而共同收益可以用存活与后代来衡量。

senses.title: Partnership between organizations
senses.definition: joint work between institutions, departments or agencies that keep their own identities
senses.definitionCN: 保持各自身份的机构、部门或机关之间的共同工作
senses.example: The museum works in cooperation with the local school.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆与当地学校合作。
senses.why: organizations cooperate rather than merge; each keeps its boundary but contributes a part, which is why the phrase in cooperation with is so common.
senses.whyCN: 机构是合作而不是合并；各方保留边界却各出一部分，因此「与……合作」这一说法极为常见。

senses.title: International and economic cooperation
senses.definition: coordinated action between countries or firms on trade, aid, research or security
senses.definitionCN: 国家或企业在贸易、援助、研究或安全上的协调行动
senses.example: The two countries signed a cooperation agreement on clean energy.
senses.exampleCN: 两国签署了一项清洁能源合作协议。
senses.why: the modern political sense scales the same division of labour up to states, where no one can compel the other and agreement must be negotiated.
senses.whyCN: 现代政治义把同一种分工放大到国家层面：任何一方都无法强迫对方，合作必须通过协商达成。

senses.title: Coordination of parts in a system
senses.definition: the way parts of a body, machine or system work together so that the whole functions
senses.definitionCN: 身体、机器或系统的各部分协同运作，使整体发挥功能
senses.example: Walking depends on the cooperation of muscles and joints.
senses.exampleCN: 行走依赖肌肉与关节的协同。
senses.why: once the word leaves people, it can describe any set of parts whose combined action produces an effect none could produce alone.
senses.whyCN: 一旦离开人，这个词就能描述任何一组部件：它们的联合动作产生单个部件无法产生的效果。

senses.title: Compliance with authority
senses.titleCN: 对执法或管理方的配合
senses.definition: the act of following instructions or allowing an official procedure to proceed
senses.definitionCN: 遵从指示或允许官方程序顺利进行
senses.example: The driver's cooperation helped the officers clear the road.
senses.exampleCN: 司机的配合帮助警员清理了道路。
senses.why: cooperation here is one-sided compliance; the word softens a demand by presenting it as shared work.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 cooperation 是单方面的顺从；这个词把一项要求说成共同工作，从而缓和了语气。

senses.title: A cooperative strategy in game theory
senses.definition: a strategy in which players choose actions that raise the joint outcome instead of competing for the larger share
senses.definitionCN: 参与者选择提高联合收益、而非争夺更大份额的策略
senses.example: In the repeated game, cooperation pays only if the other side also keeps its promise.
senses.exampleCN: 在重复博弈中，只有当对方也守约时，合作才划算。
senses.why: game theory makes the word technical: cooperation is not goodwill but a strategy that survives only under conditions of repeated contact and observable behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 博弈论把这个词技术化：合作不是善意，而是在重复接触与可观察行为条件下才存活的策略。

intro.en: Cooperation comes from Late Latin cooperari, built on com- 'together' and operari 'to work', itself from opus 'work'. It reached English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cooperation 来自晚期拉丁 cooperari，由 com-「一起」与 operari「做事」构成，而 operari 又源自 opus「工作」。它经法语进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Opus meant 'work, a piece of work'; its stem oper- supplies the verb operari 'to work, labour'.
items.cn: opus 意为「工作、一件作品」；其词干 oper- 构成动词 operari「做事、劳作」。

items.en: Cooperari combined com- 'together' with operari, meaning 'to work together, collaborate'. The prefix assimilated to co- before the vowel.
items.cn: cooperari 把 com-「一起」与 operari 组合，意为「共同做事、协作」；前缀在元音前同化为 co-。

items.en: French coopération carried the noun into English in the sixteenth or seventeenth century; cooperate followed in the same period.
items.cn: 法语 coopération 在 16 或 17 世纪把名词带入英语；动词 cooperate 也在同一时期进入。

items.en: The economic and international senses date mainly from the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, when firms, unions and states began to sign standing agreements.
items.cn: 经济与国际义主要形成于 19 与 20 世纪，当时公司、工会与国家开始签订长期协议。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English citation of cooperation is not firmly fixed, and dictionaries differ on whether the noun came straight from Latin or through French.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：cooperation 在英语中的最早书证没有确切年代；词典对名词是直接来自拉丁还是经法语而来也有分歧。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same co- plus oper- family; group two holds words that also describe joint work but differ in emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 co- 加 oper- 词族的词；第二组同样描述共同工作，但侧重不同。

entries.definition: Willing to help, or a member-owned business; it describes a quality or an entity, not the activity itself.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意配合的，或成员共有的企业；描述性质或实体，而非活动本身。

entries.definition: To run or work a machine or system; without co- there is no second agent.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器或运行系统；没有 co- 就没有第二个行动者。

entries.definition: The act of running something, or a surgical procedure; it does not require a partner.
entries.definitionCN: 运行某物，或外科手术；不需要伙伴。

entries.definition: A joint owner; the prefix is the same, but the root is own, not work.
entries.definitionCN: 共同所有人；前缀相同，但词根是 own（拥有），而非 work（工作）。

entries.definition: Working jointly, especially on a creative or intellectual project; it stresses the shared product more than the shared labour.
entries.definitionCN: 共同工作，尤指创意或学术项目；更强调共同成果而非共同劳动。

entries.definition: Organizing separate efforts so that they fit together; cooperation supplies the will, coordination the schedule.
entries.definitionCN: 把各自的努力组织到合适的位置；cooperation 提供意愿，coordination 提供时序。

entries.definition: The combined effort of a team; it is warmer and less formal than cooperation.
entries.definitionCN: 团队的合力；比 cooperation 更口语、更亲切。

entries.definition: A biological relationship in which both species benefit; the technical name for cooperation across species.
entries.definitionCN: 两个物种都获益的生物学关系；是跨物种合作的技术名称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: co- 'together' + operari 'work' = work together; the same root appears in operate and opera.
normal.cn: co-「一起」+ operari「做事」= 共同做事；同一词根也出现在 operate 与 opera 中。

normal.en: The family runs cooperate, cooperative, cooperation, cooperator and cooperatively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cooperate、cooperative、cooperation、cooperator 与 cooperatively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: close cooperation, international cooperation, in cooperation with, full cooperation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：紧密合作、国际合作、与……合作、全力配合。

normal.en: The preposition matters: in cooperation with means two parties, while with the cooperation of means one party assisting another.
normal.cn: 介词很关键：说「与……合作」时指双方，说「在某方的配合下」时指一方协助另一方。

normal.en: Biology has its own word, mutualism, for cooperation between species.
normal.cn: 生物学有专门术语「互利共生」指物种之间的合作。

abstract.en: Picture two people carrying one heavy table, each holding a different end.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人抬一张重桌，各自抓住不同的一端。

abstract.en: Picture a rowing crew whose oars enter the water on the same beat.
abstract.cn: 想象赛艇队员的桨在同一拍入水。

abstract.en: Picture a machine whose parts each do one motion so that the whole moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器，每个部件各做一个动作，整体才动起来。

examples.en: The project succeeded through close cooperation between the two labs.
examples.cn: 这个项目靠两个实验室的紧密合作而成功。

examples.en: Police thanked the public for its cooperation during the search.
examples.cn: 警方感谢公众在搜寻期间的配合。

examples.en: Clean-energy cooperation between the two countries began in the 1990s.
examples.cn: 两国的清洁能源合作始于 20 世纪 90 年代。

dict_mnemonic.text: co（一起）+ operation（操作）——几个人一起操作同一件事 → 合作

root: 拉丁晚期 cooperari「共同做事」= com-（一起）+ operari「工作」（源自 opus「工作」）。英语经法语借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep the same division of labour but change the setting: a task, a request, a species pair, two institutions, two states, a body's parts, an authority, a game.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项保持同一种分工，只更换场景：一项任务、一次请求、一对物种、两个机构、两个国家、身体各部、一个执法方、一场博弈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one load, two pairs of hands, each taking a different end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件重物，两双手，各自抬住不同的一端。

branches.en: THE CORE: a shared aim is what turns separate efforts into one act.
branches.cn: 核心：共同目标把分散的努力变成同一个动作。

branches.en: THE ATTITUDE: willingness is the door through which help enters.
branches.cn: 态度：意愿是帮助得以进入的那道门。

branches.en: ACROSS SPECIES: biology measures the shared benefit in survival.
branches.cn: 跨物种：生物学用存活来衡量共同收益。

branches.en: ACROSS BORDERS: institutions and states cooperate without merging.
branches.cn: 跨越边界：机构与国家合作而不合并。

branches.en: OTHER SHAPES: parts, compliance and strategy all keep the same division of labour.
branches.cn: 其他形态：部件、顺从与策略都保持同一种分工。

intro.en: Cooperation is a prefix-root noun: co- 'together' plus operari 'to work' plus -ation. The same root family runs through operate, operation and opera.
intro.cn: cooperation 是前缀加词根的名词：co-「一起」加 operari「做事」，再加 -ation。同一词根族贯穿 operate、operation 与 opera。

latinIntro.en: Latin opus 'work' gives operari and, with com-, cooperari; English takes cooperate, cooperation, cooperative and cooperator from this line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 opus「工作」生成 operari，并与 com- 合成 cooperari；英语由此得到 cooperate、cooperation、cooperative 与 cooperator。

items.example: Before a vowel the prefix shortens to co-.
items.exampleCN: 在元音前这个前缀缩为 co-。

items.example: Opus is the noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: opus 是整个词族背后的名词。

items.example: Operari supplies the verbal idea of labour.
items.exampleCN: operari 提供「劳作」的动词含义。

items.example: The Late Latin verb named joint labour.
items.exampleCN: 这个晚期拉丁动词命名共同劳动。
cooperari 加 -ation 命名这项活动。
合作需要一个共同目标。

items.example: The two teams agreed to cooperate.

items.meaning: tending to work together; a jointly owned business
items.meaningCN: 倾向于合作的；共同所有的企业
items.example: A cooperative shop is owned by its members.
items.exampleCN: 合作社商店由成员共有。

items.example: Every cooperator received a share of the harvest.
items.exampleCN: 每位合作者都分到了一份收成。

items.meaning: to work, run or perform an operation

latinEntries.structure: operari, operatus sum (deponent verb, first conjugation)

definition_en: to deal with a difficult situation or a heavy load
core_image: 一个人低着头顶着风走，衣角被吹得笔直
scene: 停水三天，邻居们轮流去远处打水。Some families coped by sharing water with their neighbours.
sceneCN: 这里 cope 指「应对」（第 1 个义项：面对困难局面并设法撑住）；句意是有些家庭靠与邻居分水来应对。

senses.title: To get through a hard time
senses.definition: to manage a difficult situation with the means you have
senses.definitionCN: 用手上有的办法撑过一个困难局面
senses.example: They coped with the loss of power for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他们撑过了一个星期没电的日子。
senses.why: A storm does not ask whether you are ready; it asks whether you can stand.
senses.whyCN: 风暴不问你准备好没有，只问你能不能站住。

senses.title: To handle a task well enough
senses.definition: to deal with a problem or duty without breaking down
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或职责处理得过去，而不至于崩掉
senses.example: She copes with three jobs and a family.
senses.exampleCN: 她要应付三份工作和一个家庭。
senses.why: Not every day is won; some are simply carried to the end.
senses.whyCN: 不是每一天都算赢，有些日子只是被撑到了尽头。

intro.en: Cope comes from Old French couper, to strike or cut, from Latin colaphus, a blow, from Greek kolaphos.
intro.cn: cope 来自古法语 couper（打、切），源于拉丁语 colaphus（一击），更早出自希腊语 kolaphos。

items.en: Kolaphos meant a blow with the fist.
items.cn: kolaphos 意为用拳头打的一击。

items.en: Colaphus kept the sense of a blow or a buffet.
items.cn: colaphus 保留了打击或掌击的含义。

items.en: Old French couper meant to strike or cut.
items.cn: 古法语 couper 意为击打或切割。

items.en: English cope first meant to fight or come to blows with someone.
items.cn: 英语 cope 最初意为与某人交手或打起来。

items.en: The sense shifted from fighting to handling a burden.
items.cn: 词义从打斗转向承担与应付。

items.en: Today it almost always appears with with.
items.cn: 今天它几乎总是与 with 一同出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short -ope shape, and the meaning group names other verbs for facing difficulty.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 -ope 外形，近义组列出其他面对困难的说法。

entries.definition: a thing made to match another
a police officer in informal speech
the range a subject or plan covers
entries.definitionCN: 某主题或计划覆盖的范围

entries.definition: to succeed in dealing with something
to deal with a situation or person
entries.definitionCN: 处理某种局面或某个人

entries.definition: to bear something painful for a long time

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a person walking into wind, then move to too many duties held at once.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一个人逆风行走开始，再到同时压来的过多职责。

normal.en: Cope almost always travels with with, because no one copes alone with nothing.
normal.cn: cope 几乎总和 with 同行，因为没人能空着手独自应付。

normal.en: The old sense was to trade blows; now you trade blows with a problem.
normal.cn: 它古时指交手；现在你是和一个问题交手。

normal.en: Think of a small boat riding a big wave: it does not stop the wave.
normal.cn: 想象小船压过大浪：它没有让浪停下。

normal.en: Coping is not winning; it is staying afloat.
normal.cn: 应对不是取胜，而是还浮在水面。

normal.en: One letter away from copy, but nothing here is copied.
normal.cn: 它和 copy 只差一个字母，但这里没有什么是抄来的。

abstract.en: Picture a walker leaning into a strong wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一个行人倾身顶着大风。

abstract.en: Picture a table piled with boxes and one steady hand beneath.
abstract.cn: 想象堆满箱子的桌子下，有一只手稳稳托着。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge holding while the river pushes.
abstract.cn: 想象河水冲压时，一座桥仍然撑住。

examples.en: He copes with pressure by running every morning.
examples.cn: 他每天早晨跑步来应对压力。

examples.en: The staff coped well when the system failed.
examples.cn: 系统出故障时，员工应付得很好。

examples.en: Some students find it hard to cope with the pace.
examples.cn: 有些学生觉得难以应付这种节奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cope 记成一个人顶着风走：风不会停，能走过去就是应付。

root: 源自希腊语 kolaphos（一拳），经拉丁语 colaphus 与古法语 couper（击打）进入英语，本指交手，后转为承担与应付。

sensesIntro.en: From trading blows with an opponent, to standing under a load that will not lift.
sensesIntro.cn: 从与对手交手，到站在一份不会变轻的重担之下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person leaning into a hard wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人倾身顶着强风。

branches.en: A hard time is met with whatever means are at hand.
branches.cn: 困难时期，用手边有的办法去迎。

branches.en: A duty is carried through without collapse.
branches.cn: 一份职责被撑到最后，人没有垮。

branches.en: Both senses are about standing while pressure stays.
branches.cn: 两个义项都关乎压力仍在时站稳。

branches.en: The first is short and sharp, like a storm.
branches.cn: 第一个义项短而急，像一场风暴。

branches.en: The second is long and quiet, like a daily load.
branches.cn: 第二个义项长而静，像每天的负担。

intro.en: Cope reached English through Old French couper, to strike, from Latin colaphus, a blow.
intro.cn: cope 经古法语 couper（击打）进入英语，源于拉丁语 colaphus（一击）。

latinIntro.en: Cope keeps company with short look-alikes such as copy and cop rather than with a Latin base.
latinIntro.cn: cope 更多与 copy、cop 这类短小形近词为伴，而没有留下常用的拉丁词基。

items.meaning: the act or way of dealing with stress
items.meaningCN: 应对压力的行为或方式

items.meaning: an easy way of avoiding a duty

items.example: A copyist made the fair copy.
items.exampleCN: 一名抄写员誊出了定稿。

definition_zh: 副本；一份；复制；抄写；模仿
definition_en: a duplicate of something, one example of a publication, or to make a duplicate
core_image: 一张纸从原件下面抽出，墨迹还带着余温
scene: 图书馆只剩一本，管理员把它复印了一份留档。She copied the page before handing the book back.
sceneCN: 这里 copy 指「复制」（第 3 个义项：做出与原物相同的另一份）；句意是她在还书之前把那一页复制了一份。

senses.title: A duplicate
senses.definition: a thing made to be exactly like another thing
senses.definitionCN: 照原物做成的一模一样的东西
senses.example: Keep a copy of your form.
senses.exampleCN: 留一份表格副本。
senses.why: The second sheet carries the same words but not the same hand.
senses.whyCN: 第二张纸带着同样的字，却不是同一只手写下的。

senses.title: One example of a publication
senses.definition: one single book, paper or record out of many printed
senses.definitionCN: 许多印本中的单独一本、一份或一张
senses.example: The shop had only two copies left.
senses.exampleCN: 店里只剩两份了。
senses.why: A print run becomes many objects, and each object is counted.
senses.whyCN: 一次印刷变成许多实物，每一件都要计数。

senses.title: To make a duplicate
senses.definition: to make something that looks the same as an original
senses.definitionCN: 做出一个与原物看起来相同的东西
senses.example: Copy the passage into your notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 把这段话抄进你的笔记本。
senses.why: Copying is following a path someone else has already walked.
senses.whyCN: 复制就是走一条别人已经走过的路。

intro.en: Copy comes from Latin copia, plenty, through Medieval Latin copia, a transcript, because copying made many texts from one.
intro.cn: copy 来自拉丁语 copia（丰富），经中世纪拉丁语 copia（抄本）演变而来，因为抄写能让一份文本变成许多份。

items.en: Copia meant abundance or a large supply.
items.cn: copia 意为丰富或大量供应。

items.en: The phrase copia libri meant an abundance of copies of a book.
items.cn: 短语 copia libri 意为某书的大量抄本。

items.en: Copia came to mean a single transcript of a text.
items.cn: copia 转而指一份文本的抄本。

items.en: Old French copie named a written copy of a document.
items.cn: 古法语 copie 指文件的书面抄本。

items.en: English copy first meant a transcript, not an original.
items.cn: 英语 copy 最初指抄本，而不是原件。

items.en: Printing and then machines widened it to any duplicate.
items.cn: 印刷术与后来的机器把它扩大到任何复制品。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short cop- base, and the meaning group names other words for making or matching a thing.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 cop- 词基，近义组列出其他表示复制或仿制的词。

entries.definition: a police officer in informal speech
to deal with a hard situation
the legal right over a work
entries.definitionCN: 对作品享有的法律权利

entries.definition: an exact second version of something
entries.definitionCN: 某物一模一样的第二份

entries.definition: to make a copy of something
to copy the way someone acts

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a second sheet under the first, then move to many printed books and to a hand following another hand.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从第一张纸下面的第二张开始，再到许多印本，最后到一只手跟着另一只手写。

normal.en: Copy begins with cop, to seize, as if the second sheet snatches the look of the first.
normal.cn: copy 开头是 cop（抓住），仿佛第二张纸抢走了第一张的样子。

normal.en: One original, many copies: the word once meant plenty.
normal.cn: 一个原件，许多副本：这个词最初就带着丰富的意思。

normal.en: A copy of a book is one object; a copy of a file is one more set of bits.
normal.cn: 一本书的一份是一件实物；一个文件的一份是一组多出来的数据。

normal.en: Copying for study is learning; copying to cheat is theft.
normal.cn: 为学习而抄是学习，为作弊而抄是偷窃。

normal.en: Remember the spelling change: copy becomes copies and copied.
normal.cn: 记住拼写变化：copy 变成 copies 与 copied。

abstract.en: Picture two sheets sliding apart with one image on both.
abstract.cn: 想象两张纸滑开，上面却是同一个图案。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of identical books side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上并排摆着一模一样的书。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tracing letters slowly under a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象灯下一只手慢慢描着字母。

examples.en: Please make three copies of this page.
examples.cn: 请把这一页复制三份。

examples.en: He copied the notes from the board.
examples.cn: 他把黑板上的笔记抄了下来。

examples.en: That dress copies a design from the sixties.
examples.cn: 那条裙子模仿了六十年代的一款设计。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 copy 记成 cop（抓）加 y：把原物的样子抓过来一份，就是复制与副本。

root: 源自拉丁语 copia（丰富），经中世纪拉丁语义项抄本与古法语 copie 演变而来，由多份抄本引申出副本与复制之义。

sensesIntro.en: From plenty of transcripts, to one printed object, and at last to the act of following an original.
sensesIntro.cn: 从大量的抄本，到单独一份印本，最后到跟随原件的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second sheet pulled from under the first.
core.cn: 核心意象：从第一张纸下面抽出的第二张纸。

branches.en: A second thing matches the first in every visible way.
branches.cn: 第二件东西在可见之处都与第一件相合。

branches.en: One printed object is counted out of a large run.

intro.en: Copy came from Latin copia, plenty, and grew the endings -er, -ist and -able in English.

latinIntro.en: The same root copia, plenty, also gives copious and copiously.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个词根 copia（丰富）也产生了 copious 与 copiously。

items.meaning: a duplicate or one printed item

items.exampleCN: 一名抄写员抄了那卷书。

items.meaning: the legal right over a work

definition_en: the central or most important part of something
core_image: 苹果被横切开，正中露出一圈整齐的籽
scene: 老师把苹果横着切开，让学生看中间那一圈小小的籽。The core of an apple holds its seeds in a small room.
sceneCN: 这里 core 指「果核」（第 2 个义项：果实中央装种子的部分）；句意是苹果的果核像一间小屋，装着它的种子。

senses.title: The central part
senses.definition: the central or most important part of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物最中心或最重要的部分
senses.example: The core of the team is its two oldest players.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍的核心是两位最年长的球员。
senses.why: Every circle needs a middle before it can have an edge.
senses.whyCN: 每个圆都要先有中心，才能有边缘。

senses.title: The seed chamber of fruit
senses.definition: the hard central part of an apple or pear that holds the seeds
senses.definitionCN: 苹果或梨中间装着种子的硬心
senses.example: Cut the apple and take out the core.
senses.exampleCN: 把苹果切开，取出果核。
senses.why: The fruit builds a small room for its seeds and calls it a core.
senses.whyCN: 果实为种子盖了一间小屋，管它叫果核。

senses.title: The central meaning
senses.definition: the central idea or meaning of an argument or a text
senses.definitionCN: 论点或文章最中心的观点或意思
senses.example: The core of her argument is simple.
senses.exampleCN: 她论点的要点很简单。
senses.why: Strip away the leaves of words and a few hard seeds remain.
senses.whyCN: 剥去话语的枝叶，剩下的就是几粒硬籽。

intro.en: Core comes from Latin cor, heart, whose stem cord- also shapes cordial and concord.
intro.cn: core 来自拉丁语 cor（心），其词干 cord- 也构成了 cordial 与 concord。

items.en: Cor meant heart, and by extension the seat of feeling.
items.cn: cor 意为心，并引申为情感的所在。

items.en: The stem cord- carried the same sense into compounds.
items.cn: 词干 cord- 把同样的意思带进了复合词。

items.en: Old French cors named the heart or the inner body.
items.cn: 古法语 cors 指心脏或身体内部。

items.en: English core first named the inner part of fruit.
items.cn: 英语 core 最初指果实内部的部分。

items.en: It now names the centre of anything, from the earth to an argument.
items.cn: 今天它指任何事物的中心，从地核到论点。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the heart base cor-, and the meaning group names other words for a centre.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示心的词基 cor-，近义组列出其他表示中心与实质的说法。

entries.definition: an organised body of people with one purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为同一目的组织起来的团体

entries.definition: a thick string or thin rope
the light bark of a tree, used for stoppers
entries.definitionCN: 一种轻软的树皮，可做瓶塞

entries.definition: the exact middle of a space
the most important part of a matter
the inner nature that makes a thing what it is
entries.definitionCN: 使事物成其为自身的内在本质

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a fruit cut open, then move to a team and to the heart of an argument.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从切开的果实开始，再到一支队伍，最后到论点的内核。

normal.en: Cor is Latin for heart, so the core is the heart of anything.
normal.cn: cor 在拉丁语里是心，所以 core 就是任何事物的心。

normal.en: An apple keeps its seeds in the core, as a house keeps its family in one room.
normal.cn: 苹果把种子留在果核里，就像房子把家人留在一间屋里。

normal.en: Cut away everything soft and the core still stands.
normal.cn: 把柔软的部分都切掉，果核还立在那里。

normal.en: A team has a core: the few people the others lean on.
normal.cn: 一支队伍有核心，就是其他人都依靠的那几个人。

normal.en: If you forget the sense, picture the hard middle you never eat.
normal.cn: 如果忘了意思，就想想那个你从不吃的硬心。

abstract.en: Picture a hard stone at the centre of a peach.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗硬核躺在桃子正中。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel whose hub holds every spoke.
abstract.cn: 想象一个轮子，轮毂把所有辐条收拢在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence with all its modifiers peeled away.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话被剥去所有修饰，只剩主干。

examples.en: The core of the city is its old square.
examples.cn: 这座城市的中心是它古老的广场。

examples.en: She cut out the core and sliced the rest.
examples.cn: 她去掉果核，把其余部分切成片。

examples.en: Honesty lies at the core of their friendship.
examples.cn: 诚实是他们友谊的核心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 core 记成「果心」：苹果正中那圈装着籽的硬心，就是整颗果子的核心。

root: 源自拉丁语 cor（心）及其属格 cordis，本指心脏，后引申为事物最中心的部分。

sensesIntro.en: From the middle of a fruit, to the middle of a room, and at last to the middle of an idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 从果实的正中，到事物的中心，最后到一个想法的内核。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fruit cut open to show its seed chamber.
core.cn: 核心意象：果实被切开，露出装籽的内室。

branches.en: The middle of a thing draws the eye first.
branches.cn: 事物的正中总是最先吸引目光。

branches.en: Fruit hides its seeds in a hard inner room.
branches.cn: 果实把种子藏在坚硬的内心室里。

branches.en: An argument also has a hard centre that must hold.
branches.cn: 一个论点也有必须立得住的硬核。

branches.en: Both name a physical middle, one abstract and one edible.
branches.cn: 两者都指物理上的中间，一个抽象，一个可食。

branches.en: From fruit to thought, the core is the part that must stay.
branches.cn: 从果实到思想，核心都是必须留下的部分。

intro.en: Core rests on Latin cor, heart, and its stem cord-, which also shapes cordial and concord.
intro.cn: core 建立在拉丁语 cor（心）及其词干 cord- 之上，cordial 与 concord 也由它构成。

latinIntro.en: The heart base cord- still beats inside cordial, concord and discord.
latinIntro.cn: 表示心的词基 cord- 至今仍活在 cordial、concord 与 discord 里。

items.example: Two cores fell into the bowl.

items.meaning: a tool that removes a core
warm and friendly from the heart

definition_en: plants like wheat or maize grown for food; the seeds of these plants
core_image: 秋天的田野里，金黄的玉米棒排满垄间
scene: 秋游时同学们钻进玉米地掰玉米，笑声此起彼伏。The farmer let us pick fresh corn in the field.
sceneCN: 这里 corn 是「玉米」（第 2 个义项：美式指玉米作物）；句意是农民让我们在地里掰新鲜玉米。

pop 与 corn 合成，义为「爆米花」

senses.title: Grain plants or their seeds
senses.definition: the seeds of grain plants such as wheat and barley, in British English
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语指小麦、大麦等谷物的种子
senses.example: The old mill ground corn into flour for bread.
senses.exampleCN: 老磨坊把谷物磨成面粉做面包。
senses.why: In Britain corn was the general word for the main local grain.
senses.whyCN: 在英国，corn 曾泛指当地主要谷物。

senses.title: Maize; the tall grain plant with yellow seeds
senses.definition: in American English, the maize plant and its yellow kernels
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语指玉米植株及黄色玉米粒
senses.example: We roasted corn on the cob at the school farm fair.
senses.exampleCN: 学校农场集市上我们烤了玉米棒。
senses.why: Settlers in America gave corn a new meaning: maize.
senses.whyCN: 美洲移民赋予 corn 新义：玉米。

senses.title: A small hard round area of skin
senses.definition: a small painful hard spot of skin, usually on a foot
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤上小的硬痛点，多在脚上
senses.example: New shoes gave him a corn on his little toe.
senses.exampleCN: 新鞋让他小脚趾磨出了鸡眼。
senses.why: A corn looks like a hard yellow seed stuck on the skin.
senses.whyCN: 鸡眼看着像粘在皮肤上的硬黄谷粒。

intro.en: Corn is a Germanic word that once meant the seed of any grain.
intro.cn: corn 是日耳曼词，曾泛指任何谷物的种子。

items.en: The Germanic root korn- meant a small hard grain.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根 korn- 意为细小坚硬的谷粒。

items.en: Norse korn shared the same seed meaning with Germanic speech.
items.cn: 北欧语 korn 与日耳曼语共有「种子」义。

items.en: Old English corn covered grain of any kind, whatever the region grew.
items.cn: 古英语 corn 泛指各类谷物，因地区而异。

items.en: British English kept the general grain meaning.
items.cn: 英式英语保留泛指谷物的用法。

items.en: American English fixed corn on maize, the New World grain.
items.cn: 美式英语把 corn 固定于玉米这一美洲谷物。

note.en: Some words share the grain family, others resemble corn in shape.
note.cn: 有的词同属谷物家族，有的形似 corn。

the centre of an apple or an idea

entries.definitionCN: 玉米淀粉（corn 与 flour 合成）

normalIntro.en: Remember corn as the seed word that changed continents.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 corn 是跨大陆变义的「种子」词。

normal.en: corn in Britain means grain in general.
normal.cn: 在英国 corn 泛指谷物。

normal.en: corn in America means maize.

normal.en: popcorn = pop + corn, corn that pops.
normal.cn: popcorn 由 pop 加 corn 构成，会爆的玉米。

normal.en: a corn on the foot looks like a seed.

normal.en: corn sounds like ken; you can (ken) eat corn on the cob.
normal.cn: corn 发音像「啃」，抱着玉米棒大口地啃。

abstract.en: Picture golden maize fields waving in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象金黄玉米田迎风摇摆。

abstract.en: Picture popcorn jumping in a hot pan.
abstract.cn: 想象爆米花在热锅里蹦跳。

abstract.en: Picture a millstone turning with grain inside.
abstract.cn: 想象磨盘转动碾着谷物。

examples.en: We bought roasted corn from a stall near the school gate.
examples.cn: 我们在校门口的小摊买了烤玉米。

examples.en: Popcorn is the best snack for a class movie afternoon.
examples.cn: 爆米花是班级观影日最好的零食。

examples.en: The grain store sells corn, wheat and beans.
examples.cn: 粮店出售玉米、小麦和豆子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啃」——抱着玉米棒一口一口地啃。

root: 日耳曼词根 korn-（谷粒；种子），与德语 Korn、荷兰语 korein 同源。英式泛指谷物，美式专指玉米。

sensesIntro.en: From any grain seed to maize and a foot corn.
sensesIntro.cn: 从泛指谷粒到玉米与脚上鸡眼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small hard grain seed

branches.en: Grain seeds in British usage.

intro.cn: corn 因指常见食物而极易构词。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic, so there are no Latin relatives here.

items.example: Cornflakes with milk is a quick breakfast.

items.meaning: a grain for beer and food

definition_zh: 角落；街角；拐角；把…逼入绝境
definition_en: the point where two lines or surfaces meet, or to force someone into a place with no escape
core_image: 两面墙相遇，挤出一个九十度的尖角
scene: 小猫被门和墙夹住，退无可退，只好弓起背。The cat was cornered between the door and the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 corner 指「把…逼入绝境」（第 3 个义项：使某人无处可退）；句意是猫被门和墙夹在角落里。

senses.title: An inside angle
senses.definition: the place inside a room where two walls or edges meet
senses.definitionCN: 房间内两堵墙或两条边相接的地方
senses.example: There is an old chair in the corner of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 房间角落里有一把旧椅子。
senses.why: Two walls meet and leave a small pocket that holds what we hide.
senses.whyCN: 两堵墙相接，留下一个小口袋，收藏我们藏起来的东西。

senses.title: The bend of a street
senses.definition: the point where two streets meet
senses.definitionCN: 两条街道相接的地方
senses.example: A small shop stands on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 街角有一家小商店。
senses.why: A street corner is where one path hands you over to another.
senses.whyCN: 街角是一条路把你交给另一条路的地方。

senses.title: To trap someone
senses.definition: to force a person or animal into a place from which there is no escape
senses.definitionCN: 把人或动物逼到无路可退的地方
senses.example: The dog cornered the cat under the car.
senses.exampleCN: 狗把猫逼到了车底下。
senses.why: A corner has two walls, so the hunted thing has only one way left.
senses.whyCN: 角落有两面墙，被追的东西只剩下一条路。

intro.en: Corner goes back to Latin cornu, a horn or pointed tip, through Old French corniere, a projecting corner.
intro.cn: corner 可追溯到拉丁语 cornu（角、尖头），经古法语 corniere（突出的角）进入英语。

items.en: Cornu meant a horn or any pointed end.
items.cn: cornu 意为兽角或任何尖出的末端。

items.en: The same word named the wing of an army.
items.cn: 同一个词也用来指军队的侧翼。

items.en: Corniere named the projecting corner of a building.
items.cn: corniere 指建筑物向外突出的角。

items.en: English corner first meant a sheltered or hidden angle.
items.cn: 英语 corner 最初指可以遮蔽、藏身的角。

items.en: It now covers room corners, street corners and tight spots with no way out.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖房间的角、街角，以及无路可退的困境。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words in -orn or -or, and the meaning group names other kinds of bend and hiding place.
note.cn: 形近组收集以 -orn 或 -or 结尾的短词，近义组列出其他表示转折与藏身处的说法。

a small brass musical instrument
the grain of a cereal plant
the space between two meeting lines

entries.definition: a small sheltered corner of a room

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two walls meeting, then move to a street bend and to an animal with no way out.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两面墙相接开始，再到街道的转弯，最后到无路可退的动物。

normal.en: Corner begins like corn, but it is the sharp end of a wall.
normal.cn: corner 开头像 corn，但它指的是墙的尖角。

normal.en: A corner is where two straight lines decide to meet.
normal.cn: 角落就是两条直线决定相遇的地方。

normal.en: Shops love corners because two streets bring two crowds.
normal.cn: 商店喜欢街角，因为两条街带来两股人流。

normal.en: If someone is cornered, every wall is behind them.
normal.cn: 如果一个人被逼到角落，每面墙都在他身后。

normal.en: Cutting corners saves time now and costs more later.
normal.cn: 偷工减料现在省时间，以后却要付出更多。

abstract.en: Picture a mouse pressed into the angle of two walls.
abstract.cn: 想象一只老鼠被挤进两面墙形成的夹角。

abstract.en: Picture a road that turns and hides what comes next.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路拐了弯，把后面的景象藏起来。

abstract.en: Picture a page folded so that one point creases hard.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸被折起，有一个点折出硬痕。

examples.en: There is a lamp in the corner of the room.

sensesIntro.en: From an angle inside a room, to the bend of a street, and at last to the trap that such an angle makes.
sensesIntro.cn: 从房间内的夹角，到街道的转弯，最后到这种夹角造成的困境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two walls meeting at a sharp right angle.

branches.en: The angle inside a room holds chairs, lamps and hidden things.

branches.en: A street corner gathers two flows of people into one point.

branches.en: The same shape that shelters can also trap.

senses.example: Please correct the second sentence on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 请改正黑板上的第二个句子。
senses.why: A small hand movement can pull a crooked line straight.
senses.whyCN: 一个小小的手势，就能把歪线拉直。

senses.title: To mark errors
senses.definition: to read work and mark the mistakes in it
senses.definitionCN: 阅读作业并标出其中的错误
senses.example: She corrects papers every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天晚上批改试卷。
senses.why: A teacher's red mark is a small bridge back to the right answer.
senses.whyCN: 老师的红笔批注，是回到正确答案的一座小桥。

intro.en: Correct comes from Latin corrigere, to make straight, built from com-, together, and regere, to rule or guide straight.
intro.cn: correct 来自拉丁语 corrigere（使变直），由 com-（一起）与 regere（引导、使直）构成。

items.en: Regere meant to guide or keep something straight.
items.cn: regere 意为引导或使某物保持笔直。

items.en: Corrigere meant to straighten what had bent.
items.cn: corrigere 意为把弯掉的东西弄直。

items.en: Correctus meant made straight or set right.
items.cn: correctus 意为被弄直、被纠正的。

items.en: English correct first described a straight rule or a right form.
items.cn: 英语 correct 最初形容笔直的规则或正确的形式。

items.en: It now judges answers, manners and even wording.
items.cn: 今天它用来判断答案、举止乃至措辞是否正确。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin straight base rect-, and the meaning group names other words for being right.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语表示直的词基 rect-，近义组列出其他表示正确的说法。

entries.definition: to gather things together
going straight without turning
to build or set upright
true or in accordance with fact
exact and free from small errors
suitable for the situation

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a straightened line, then move to a teacher's red pen and to a corrected answer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被拉直的线开始，再到老师的红笔，最后到改对的答案。

normal.en: Regere is to rule a straight line, so correct means made straight.
normal.cn: regere 是画出直线，所以 correct 就是被弄直。

normal.en: A correct answer stands up without leaning on excuses.
normal.cn: 正确答案站得直，不必靠在借口上。

normal.en: The two c letters hold the word in a straight frame.
normal.cn: 两个 c 像画框，把这个词夹在笔直的框里。

normal.en: To correct a paper is to move each wrong mark one step back.
normal.cn: 批改试卷，就是把每个错号往回挪一步。

normal.en: Correct and direct both keep the straight base rect.
normal.cn: correct 与 direct 都保留着表示直的词基 rect。

abstract.en: Picture a bent wire pulled straight by two fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象一根弯铁丝被两根手指拉直。

abstract.en: Picture a red cross turning into a neat tick.
abstract.cn: 想象一个红叉慢慢变成一个整齐的勾。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid along a crooked row of letters.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子压在一行歪斜的字母上。

examples.en: Only one of the four answers is correct.
examples.cn: 四个答案里只有一个是对的。

examples.en: The teacher corrected our spelling mistakes.
examples.cn: 老师改正了我们的拼写错误。

examples.en: He corrects papers late into the night.
examples.cn: 他批改试卷一直到深夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 correct 记成 cor 加 rect（直）：把弯的东西扳成直线，就是改正、使正确。

root: 源自拉丁语 corrigere（使变直、纠正），由 com-（一起）与 regere（引导、使直）构成，本指把弯的东西弄直，后引申为正确与改正。

sensesIntro.en: From a line made straight, to an error put right, and at last to the work of marking errors for others.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被弄直的线，到被改对的错误，最后到替别人标出错误的工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red pen pulling a crooked stroke back to a straight line.
core.cn: 核心意象：红笔把歪斜的一笔拉回笔直的线上。

branches.en: A fact or form agrees with the standard and stands straight.
branches.cn: 事实或形式与标准相符，笔直地立着。

branches.en: A wrong thing is bent back into its right shape.
branches.cn: 错误的东西被扳回正确的形状。

branches.en: Marking is correcting done for someone else.
branches.cn: 批改就是替别人做的纠正。

branches.en: The state of being right and the act of making right share one root.
branches.cn: 正确这一状态与改对这一动作共用一个词根。

branches.en: Both move a piece of work one step toward the standard.
branches.cn: 两者都把一份作业朝标准推近一步。

intro.en: Correct is built on Latin regere, to guide straight, with the prefix com-, giving the sense of making straight.
intro.cn: correct 建立在拉丁语 regere（引导、使直）之上，加上前缀 com-，得到使变直的意思。

latinIntro.en: The straight base rect- also appears in direct, erect and rectangle.
latinIntro.cn: 表示直的词基 rect- 也出现在 direct、erect 与 rectangle 中。

items.meaning: a change that puts something right

items.example: He doubts the correctness of the claim.
items.exampleCN: 他怀疑这个说法的正确性。
